name: 0H10M1ke
bio: 0H10M1ke is a Brooklyn-based interdisciplinary artist known as “The One-Line Master,” recognized for creating more than 15,000 live portraits and light-based performances across cities including New York, Miami, Tokyo, Kyoto, and Berlin. Working at the intersection of drawing, performance, and light, he translates real-time gesture into luminous forms using a Wacom tablet and stylus, treating each mark as an immediate, unrepeatable response to the moment. His ongoing series L1ght Graff1t1 Make0vers transforms participants into vivid, reimagined identities through live digital light performance, blending street aesthetics, improvisation, and spectacle. Across international exhibitions at venues such as the Park Avenue Armory, the Guggenheim Museum, and the Museum of Graffiti, his work explores light as both medium and metaphor for connection, impermanence, and shared human presence.

At Cintrifuse, she stewards the StartupCincy community - convening entrepreneurs, investors, support organizations, and community partners to move Cincinnati’s innovation ecosystem forward and ultimately advance the region as a whole.

Her passion for building a more connected, vibrant Cincinnati extends to her role as Vice Chair of the OTR Chamber of Commerce, and Founder of RADICO, a civic impact studio taking bold concepts from idea to action. Across her work, she’s happiest at the intersection of big dreams, interesting people, and making Cincinnati the best place to build and to thrive.

name: Adam Bianco
title: Founder & Chief Strategist
bio: Adam Bianco is the Founder & Chief Strategist at Offtrail Marketing, an email and lifecycle marketing agency that helps businesses onboard new customers, increase retention, create more personalized customer journeys, and more. He’s also the host of the AI-Powered Inbox podcast, which shares proven strategies for implementing AI in lifecycle marketing. Adam has over 15 years of marketing experience working with top B2B and B2C brands, ranging from Fortune 50 companies to startups, including P&G, The Beard Club, and the national nonprofit Move For Hunger. Along the way, he has launched campaigns in partnership with iconic brands such as Harley-Davidson, Disney, the Chicago Cubs, Kroger, the NFL, and more. He’s also a proud dad of 1-year-old identical twin boys.

name: Aérosculpture
bio: Inspired by airships and the dream of flight, Jean-Pierre David creates immersive artworks that explore the possibilities of aerostatic forms, light, and movement. Since the mid-1990s, he has developed inflatable sculptures, aerial performances, and illuminated installations that combine suspended performers, giant puppets, music, and visual spectacle. As advances in LED technology enabled light to become an integral part of his work, he expanded into increasingly sophisticated creations that merge digital systems, electromechanics, transparency, and motion. His large-scale installations invite audiences into imaginative worlds where art, technology, and the wonder of floating converge.

name: Aftab Pureval
title: Mayor
bio:
Aftab Pureval is the 70th Mayor of Cincinnati. He was raised in Southwest, Ohio, the son of first-generation Americans. He is making history as Cincinnati’s first Asian- American Mayor. He has made equitable economic growth a top priority of his administration, as well as a comprehensive reform and improvement of public safety, affordable housing, and environmental action.

Since taking office, Mayor Aftab has guided Cincinnati through a significant economic recovery, while advancing the City’s key strategic priorities for equitable growth.

Early accomplishments include establishing the City’s first-ever annual commitment to an affordable housing trust fund, leading on a comprehensive zoning reform to bring more housing options to neighborhoods, and implementing a new policy to send unarmed mental health professionals to some nonviolent 911 calls. Under his leadership, the City’s budget was balanced after multiple years of structural deficits, and the City committed for the first time to carbon neutrality by 2050.

Since joining Model in 2023, she has guided leasing, tenant partnerships, and ground-floor activation across neighborhoods including Over-the-Rhine, Pendleton, Findlay Market, Walnut Hills, and Downtown. Alex began her career in New York City’s fashion industry before transitioning to real estate in 2017. She is a Cincinnati resident and active member of the urban core community.

name: Ali Crowdus
title: Founder, Consultant
bio: Chef Ali Crowdus, a Northern Kentucky native, is the founder of The People’s Kitchen, a consultancy providing strategic advising for small food businesses. With almost two decades in the hospitality industry, Ali is a seasoned chef, entrepreneur, community leader, and an advocate for local food makers. Ali is also the President of Chef & Coffee, a non-profit organization supporting Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky’s culinary community. Outside of work Ali spends time with her daughter Nora, volunteering, going to concerts, experiencing art, and exploring new local makers.

name: Allison Schroeder
title: Founder
bio: Allison Schroeder, APR is an award-winning public relations professional with nearly 20 years of experience serving in both agency and in-house roles. Allison is the founder of Pomme Communications, an agency specializing in public relations, marketing activations and strategic partnerships. Under her leadership, Pomme has been recognized more than 30 times for its work in the industry, representing clients within the food, beverage and hospitality space. In the community, Allison is actively involved in the Public Relations Society of America, having served a number of board roles, including President, and is currently the Director of Accreditation. She is also involved with the Ohio State Alumni Association of Cincinnati, where she has served on several committees. She is also particularly passionate about giving back to support local cancer research, as demonstrated through her involvement with Ride Cincinnati and the Cincinnati Cancer Advisors. She is a regular presenter at Aviatra Accelerators, serves as a coach for Sam Adams Brewing the American Dream program and has created programming for private organizations as well as conferences, including Startup Cincy Week, Cincinnati PRSA Media day, and the 2025 ICON PRSA national conference in Washington DC. Most notably, Allison is the 2021 recipient of the Werner-Vonderhaar-Bogart Award, Cincinnati PRSA’s highest honor for contributions to the profession and the community. Pomme is the 2024 and 2025 recipient of Small Agency of the Year and has been recognized as “Best in Cincy” for several years. In addition, Allison is the creator of the online series, The Creativity is Human Project, in which she sits down with creatives of all varieties to learn more about their unique creative processes and prove that the best creative ideas are derived from uniquely human experiences. Allison hold a B.A. from The Ohio State University and can be found on Saturdays cheering on her beloved Buckeyes at the weekly game watch.

name: Allyson West
title: Executive Director/Founder
bio:
Allyson West is an award-winning filmmaker, producer, director, performer, and the founder and executive director of the Cindependent Film Festival in Cincinnati, Ohio. A native Texan, West earned her BFA in Acting from the University of Cincinnati’s College-Conservatory of Music (CCM) before moving to New York City to pursue a career in performance. She later returned to Cincinnati, where her experiences as a performer and independent filmmaker inspired her to create new opportunities for artists in the region.

West began making her own films after struggling to find consistent acting work. Her 2016 short film Texican, which she wrote, produced, directed, and performed in, went on to screen at numerous film festivals and receive multiple awards and nominations. The experience exposed her to independent filmmaking communities around the country and ultimately led her to envision a film festival that would give Cincinnati filmmakers and visiting artists a dedicated platform.

In 2018, West founded the Cindependent Film Festival, an organization dedicated to creating a home for independent filmmaking in Cincinnati. As executive director, she has worked to build a community around independent film while providing filmmakers with opportunities for education, professional development, networking, and exhibition. The festival has grown into a significant part of Cincinnati’s independent film community.

Known for her entrepreneurial spirit, collaborative approach, and passion for storytelling, West focuses on creating meaningful connections between filmmakers, audiences, and the broader Cincinnati community. Her work reflects a belief that independent film can not only tell compelling stories but also strengthen communities and create opportunities for emerging creative voices.

name: Amelia Wares
title: Founder
bio: Amelia is a senior biomedical engineering student at the University of Cincinnati. She is the Founder of TissuTrak, a mobile app for patients with Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (hEDS) and Long-COVID that helps patients identify correlations between lifestyle factors and their symptoms so they can have better communication with their doctors and eventually feel better.

name: Amy Vaughan
title: CEO / Managing Director
bio: I’m a builder of brands, leaders, and communities — with a healthy rebel streak and a deep belief that how we work matters just as much as what we create. With 15+ years of enterprise creative leadership, I’ve led award-winning campaigns for global brands like Ford, P&G, Walmart, Humana, and Gillette, blending strategic clarity with bold creative execution. My work lives at the intersection of purpose, performance, and people — pushing boundaries while delivering real results. Today, my work is focused on something even bigger: creating environments where people thrive. As CEO of Together Digital, I lead a national platform empowering 500+ women in digital and tech through strategic networking, mentorship, and an ask-and-give community model designed to drive real career outcomes — raises, promotions, and access to opportunity. As Managing Director of The Marketer Collaborative, I’m building a physical space rooted in the belief that community fuels momentum. It’s a coworking and event environment intentionally designed for marketers, creatives, and business builders who want more than a desk — they want connection, inspiration, and room to grow.

name: Ana Tomashvili
bio: This Georgian artist works at the intersection of architecture, sound, and moving image, reimagining buildings and public spaces through light, projection, and immersive soundscapes. Their practice transforms static structures into dynamic, emotional environments that invite audiences into moments of awe and heightened perception. Rooted in a fascination with wonder and presence, their work uses synchronized light and sound to slow time and expand sensory awareness. Through a blend of architectural precision and poetic rhythm, they create immersive experiences that encourage reflection and a renewed connection to the beauty of the surrounding world.

name: Andrew Caprariello
title: Senior Consultant
bio:
Andrew is a brain scientist seeking to bridge the gap between basic and applied research. With a keen eye for win-win opportunity, he has led worldwide research collaborations, chaired preeminent conferences, and has advised companies both for-profit and not.

As Fractional CEO of Zafer Tx, he oversees corporate strategy, partnerships, and fundraising to advance Zafer’s platform from preclinical proof-of-concept in lupus-inspired models to first-in-human studies in ANCA-associated vasculitis.

Andrew is a Senior Consultant at Wave Strategy LLC and Owner/Principal of Cap Consulting LLC. Previously, he was CEO of 4P-Pharma USA, and Director of Biology at Convelo Therapeutics. He did his Postdoctoral training in Clinical Neurosciences at the University of Calgary Cumming School of Medicine (Canada). He holds a PhD in Physiology & Biophysics from Case Western Reserve University and a BA in Neuroscience from Oberlin College.

With a background spanning urban planning, clean-tech, tech transfer, and civic innovation, Antony focuses on cultivating resilient, interconnected networks where entrepreneurs transform ambitious ideas into lasting regional impact.

name: Barbara Hauser
title: Community Advocate
bio:
Barbara Hauser has spent her career strengthening the fabric of Cincinnati’s arts and nonprofit community. After 18 years at Procter & Gamble—including 14 as Community Relations Manager—she led regional giving, sponsorships, nonprofit partnerships, and D&I engagement, ensuring P&G’s community investments reflected the city’s diverse voices.

Her roots in the arts run deep. Barbara previously served as director of marketing for Cincinnati Ballet, director of communications for the YMCA of Greater Cincinnati, and a PR account manager at the Powers Agency. Today, she continues to shape the cultural landscape through her work on the 1001 Colors Board and the ArtsWave 100 Anniversary Committee.

Barbara is driven by the belief that art should be accessible to everyone. She founded The Red Door Project, a pop‑up gallery that elevates local artists and celebrates creativity across the community.

name: Batres Gilvin
title: Artist collaborative (Karla Batres and Bradly Gilvin)
bio: Batres Gilvin, an artist collaborative in Greater Cincinnati, is comprised of Karla Batres and Bradly Gilvin, life partners who met in 2011 while studying at the Art Academy of Cincinnati. In a multiethnic partnership that joins the personal with the professional, Batres’ Mexican American heritage and Gilvin’s Southern American roots are a catalyst for complicated conversations about difference, otherness, and identity. In their Morning View, Kentucky studio located on the property of the Gilvin family farm and homestead, Batres Gilvin explores the local and global implications of immigration. Their artistic work is informed as much by larger political conversations as it is by life on the farm and daily interactions with Bradly and Karla’s immediate and extended family.

name: Beamhacker
bio: Beamhacker is a light installation artist whose practice explores the space where technology meets imagination and strives to spark curiosity and transform human perception. With roots in the events industry, his early work embraced a lo-fi, set-design aesthetic before evolving into more complex, technology driven artworks that merge DIY electronics with cutting-edge systems. His installations have employed LED, fibre optics, lasers, video projection, VR, and interactive sensors to create immersive environments that blur the boundary between the physical and the imagined.

bio: The lady in purple, you can’t miss her. That’s Bethany George, owner and founder of The Sales Mystique. With decades of sales experience, Bethany helps small business owners and B2B professionals stop following scripts that don’t fit and start selling in a way that feels natural to them. Her clients describe the same shift: from dreading every sales conversation to approaching them with calm confidence, not because they learned a new script, but because they finally started selling as themselves. Practical, playful, and genuinely invested in your success.

name: Betty Poling
title: Director of Food Innovation
bio: Betty Poling is a nonprofit and small business leader with extensive experience in food entrepreneurship, workforce development, organizational leadership, and community-based economic development. She is a Certified Professional through the Society for Human Resource Management and currently serves as Director of Food Innovation at the Corporation for Findlay Market, where she supports entrepreneurs through programs including Findlay Kitchen, Findlay Launch, and Findlay Learn. Previously, Betty co-founded Fibonacci Brewing Company in 2015 and served as its President, leading the business through nearly a decade of growth and the expansion of its urban farm and hospitality ventures. Under her leadership, Fibonacci became the first brewery to participate in Ellequate’s workplace equity certification program. Her background also includes more than 10 years in the craft beer industry and 11 years in restaurant and hospitality operations. Betty has been actively involved in community and economic development throughout Greater Cincinnati. She has served as Cincinnati Chapter Leader of the Pink Boots Society and Vice President of the Mount Healthy Business Association, and helped address local food insecurity through Mount Healthy’s We Thrive initiative, including the development of a community farmers market. Across her work, Betty is passionate about strengthening small businesses, expanding opportunity, and building programs and communities where people and ideas can thrive.

name: Big Art
bio: Big Art exists to ignite imagination and wonder through large-scale, interactive, and immersive public art installations. With a purpose rooted in inspiring creativity, we craft experiences that captivate audiences, spark curiosity, and transform public spaces into vibrant playgrounds for exploration. Our team designs, builds, and tours robust, safe, and unforgettable installations across North America, whether through our existing catalogue or custom commissions.

name: Black Art Speaks
bio: Black Art Speaks (BAS) is a Cincinnati-based nonprofit, membership-driven artist collective dedicated to promoting Black culture, social justice, and creative expression through the elevation of Black artists' voices. Founded in 2020, the organization brings together artists, community leaders, and advocates who use art as a catalyst for dialogue, healing, and community impact. BAS is best known for creating Cincinnati's iconic Black Lives Matter mural and has since developed numerous public art initiatives, exhibitions, educational programs, and professional development opportunities for Black artists. Through collaboration, advocacy, and public art, Black Art Speaks continues to foster cultural awareness, create economic opportunities for artists, and strengthen communities throughout Greater Cincinnati.

name: Brett Bolton
bio: Brett Bolton is an audiovisual artist from Las Vegas who creates tightly connected musical and visual systems and then controls them live with drums and a touchpad. Every drum hit, synth line, and ambient swell is tied directly to a visual element, allowing each AV song to be as dynamic, improvised, and imperfect as the human that drives it. Given the real-time generative nature of the AV systems he builds, every performance is a completely unique collaboration between computer and human that exists only in that moment and can never be perfectly replicated. When he’s not building personal work, Brett designs visuals and real-time systems for touring pop artists, XR stages, and cutting-edge venues.

name: Calvin Davis
title: Donor Engagement Manager
org: Cincinnati Art Museum/Cincinnati Young Black Professionals
bio:
Calvin Davis is a passionate advocate for minority empowerment and community development. A two-time Miami University graduate, Calvin earned his Bachelor's in Marketing in 2014 and his Master's in Business Administration in 2023. He currently serves as the Donor Engagement Manager at the Cincinnati Art Museum, where he strengthens relationships to support cultural enrichment.

Beyond his professional role, Calvin is deeply involved in advancing opportunities for Black professionals and underrepresented communities. He co-chairs Cincinnati Young Black Professionals and serves on the Young Professionals Board for Cincinnati Youth Collaborative. Recognizing his passion for advancing the city's and region's most vulnerable, the mayor of Cincinnati and City Council appointed him to the city's Human Services Advisory Committee.

In his free time, Calvin also mentors, both formally through the LevelUp mentorship program and informally through the connections he has cultivated. As the co-founder of the Analog Cincy event series and in his other endeavors, Calvin is committed to creating inclusive spaces where individuals can connect, network, and thrive authentically. His leadership and dedication reflect his mission to inspire growth, amplify voices, and foster equity in all facets of community life.

name: Candida Crasto
title: Founder, Executive Director
bio: Candida Crasto, MFT, LPC (she/her) is the Founder and Executive Director of The AFFECT Project, a non-profit clinical research initiative developing an evidence-backed model for integrated sex and family therapy. A former chemical engineer who navigated the startup world before becoming a licensed therapist, Candida bridges analytical systems-thinking with deep human connection. She is also the host of the #SEXHAPPENS podcast, where she destigmatizes sexuality through candid, shame-busting conversations. Across her research, podcast, and experiential workshops, Candida helps individuals, couples, and families dismantle internal barriers, step into their authentic selves, and step into their full potential.

name: Carmen Winant
title: Artist and Roy Lichtenstein Chair of Studio Art at the Ohio State University
bio: Carmen Winant is an artist and the Roy Lichtenstein Chair of Studio Art at the Ohio State University. Her work utilizes archival and authored photographs to examine feminist care networks, with particular emphasis on intergenerational, multiracial, and sometimes transnational coalition building. Winant’s recent projects have been shown at The Museum of Modern Art, New York, NY; Muzeum Sztuki Nowoczesnej, Warsaw, Poland; the Whitney Museum of American Art, New York, NY; the Minneapolis Institute of Art, MN; SculptureCenter, Queens NY; Wexner Center for the Arts, Columbus, OH; the Institute of Contemporary Art, Boston, MA; the Cleveland Museum of Art, OH; and el Museo Universitario Arte Contemporáneo, Mexico City, Mexico. Winant’s artist’s books include My Birth (2018), Notes on Fundamental Joy (2019), Instructional Photography: Learning How To Live Now (2021), Arrangements (2022), A Brand New End: Survival and Its Pictures (2022), and The Last Safe Abortion (2024). Winant is a 2019 Guggenheim Fellow in photography, a 2020 Foundation of Contemporary Arts Artist Honoree, and a 2021 American Academy of Arts and Letters award recipient. She is also a community organizer, prison educator, and mother. (Photo Credit: Jordan Weitzman)

name: Casey Sprague
title: Founder
bio:
Casey Sprague is the Founder and CEO of SpectC Technologies Inc, a Cincinnati-area startup building an Execution Intelligence platform that helps organizations turn strategy into measurable execution. SpectC gives leaders greater visibility into project health, risk, priorities, and performance so teams can identify problems earlier and make better decisions faster.

Casey brings more than 15 years of experience across technology, aerospace and defense, SaaS, project and program management, and organizational leadership. A retired U.S. Army Major, PMP, CSM, and Georgetown University graduate, he has built his career around solving complex execution challenges and helping teams move from planning to results.

He is also the owner of Constructive Curiosity, a project management, training, and advisory firm, and is passionate about building companies, developing people, and contributing to Cincinnati’s growing startup ecosystem.

name: Catherine Jue
title: Co-Founder
bio: Catherine Jue is the co-founder and CEO of Kernel, an AI infrastructure company building the browser layer that allows AI agents to interact with the internet. Founded in 2025 and part of Y Combinator’s S25 cohort, Kernel has raised $22 million in Seed and Series A funding led by Accel. A repeat founder and technologist, Catherine previously co-founded Sway Finance (YC S16) and went on to lead engineering teams at Cash App, including its forward-deployed engineering team and developer documentation platform. She studied linguistics and computer science at UCLA and brings a career-long focus on building technology at the intersection of infrastructure, automation, and emerging platforms.

name: Catherine Lentz
title: Director of Lending, Southern Ohio
bio: Catherine Lentz is the Director of Lending for Southern Ohio at Economic and Community Development Institute (ECDI). She helps entrepreneurs and small business owners realize their dream of owning and growing their small business by providing resources and small business financing. Catherine has over 25 years of experience in the financial services industry and prior to joining ECDI in 2021, she was a Business Relationship Manager and Private Client Branch Manager with JPMorgan Chase. Catherine grew up in the Dayton, Ohio area, is a graduate of the University of Cincinnati, Co-Chair of the Emerging Leaders for the Cincinnati Parks Foundation and a sustaining member of the Junior League of Cincinnati.

name: Chase Melendez
bio: This artist’s work is formally inspired by the aesthetics of early video games, 1980s and 1990s cartoons, and cinema, with a focus on color, background art, and narrative-driven visual storytelling. They have developed a personal visual language called “Candy Pop Sci-Fi Abstraction,” using it as a framework for worldbuilding through vibrant color combinations, sharp geometric forms, and layered compositions. Their work spans painting, object-based surfaces, and immersive installations that aim to activate space, reimagine overlooked environments, and create playful, energetic visual experiences for the public. Raised in the Pacific Northwest and currently based in Cincinnati’s Camp Washington neighborhood, they hold an MFA from the University of Cincinnati and a BA from San Diego State University, alongside experience in event production, film, and theater.

name: Chaske Haverkos
bio: Chaske Haverkos is a director, immersive designer, 3D animator, and projection-mapping artist from Cincinnati, Ohio, whose work spans advertising, creative production, and experiential entertainment. A graduate of the University of Cincinnati’s DAAP program, he brings over 15 years of experience collaborating with clients, organizations, and public entities to create visually rich and technologically driven experiences for audiences of all sizes. His practice fuses traditional design principles with emerging technologies, combining animation, motion graphics, and projection mapping to craft immersive audiovisual environments. Working as a freelance artist, he continues to explore the digital frontier of light and sound, developing experiential works that translate artistic vision into dynamic, spatial storytelling.

name: Chris Bergman
title: Founder/CEO
bio: Chris Bergman is a serial entrepreneur, game creator, and investor based in Cincinnati, Ohio. He is the founder and CEO of Gylee Games, an independent studio focused on creating character-driven games with distinctive worlds and meaningful stories, and served as game director, writer, designer, and composer on the studio’s debut title, Ra Ra BOOM. Previously, Chris co-founded ChoreMonster, a family-focused technology company that grew to more than four million users and participated in the Disney Accelerator. He is also a General Partner at Everywhere Ventures Midwest, where he supports early-stage founders and helps strengthen the region’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. His multidisciplinary career spans technology, venture capital, video games, music, and Cincinnati’s creative community. All connected by a belief that meaningful work can also be weird, joyful, and deeply human.

Christopher A. Ritter is a design thinker, branding expert, and creative entrepreneur focused on strategy, identity, and cultural relevance.

He’s led brand work for adidas, GE, lululemon, and the Chicago Cubs, and created public art and exhibitions alongside artists like FAILE, The London Police, and Gene Spatz. His practice integrates strategy and design to help brands evolve and is grounded in the future of creative leadership.

name: Christin Godale
title: Executive Director
bio: Dr. Christin Godale is a scientist, innovation strategist, and ecosystem builder with experience spanning academic research, venture capital, early-stage company development, and nonprofit innovation infrastructure. Trained as a neuroscientist, she brings a dual perspective as an academically trained scientist and a builder of programs, partnerships, and platforms that help scientific innovation move into the real world. She is the founding Executive Director of LifeSciKY, a nonprofit life sciences lab in Kentucky, where she leads strategy, partnerships, and infrastructure development to support early-stage biotech, diagnostics, and health innovation companies while strengthening the life sciences ecosystem. Christin’s expertise spans therapeutics, cell and gene therapy, neurology, drug-delivery systems, and emerging biomedical technologies. She is known for translating complex science into clear, actionable strategy and for aligning research, venture insight, policy, capital, and talent to accelerate impact. She is deeply passionate about using innovation infrastructure as an economic development tool, expanding access to labs, talent pathways, and STEM education, reducing barriers for scientists and founders, and ensuring that breakthrough research can create jobs, companies, and healthier communities, especially in regions that have historically been overlooked.

name: Christina Moss
title: Managing Partner/Founder
bio: Christina S. Moss, CPA is the founder of MossFinancials, LLC, a CPA-led advisory and accounting firm that helps business owners uncover what’s actually true about their businesses so they can make better decisions and lead with greater confidence. With more than 25 years of accounting experience, Christina has seen firsthand that many of the challenges entrepreneurs face with money aren't simply accounting problems. They're decision-making problems shaped by uncertainty, fear, overwhelm, and the stories we tell ourselves about our businesses. A passionate financial educator and advocate for underserved entrepreneurs, Christina uses accounting as a tool to replace uncertainty with clarity and help founders move from reacting to leading. Her candid, compassionate, and no-nonsense approach to money, growth, and business decision-making has earned her the nickname “The PitBull of Accounting™.”

name: Christo Squier & Thomas Blackburn
bio:
Christo Squier is a composer, installation artist, and creative director whose work explores the intersection of music, science, and immersive experience. Drawing on fields such as particle physics and cognitive science, he creates generative environments that investigate perception, energy, and the boundaries between the tangible and intangible. His practice blends electronic and classical composition with installation, performance, and interactive systems, and he has collaborated with companies including Punchdrunk, Secret Cinema, and Les Enfants Terribles. He has also received commissions from Science Gallery London and Britten Pears Arts, along with awards for innovation in immersive sound.

Thomas Blackburn is a creative code and audiovisual specialist with over 20 years of experience designing and programming complex audiovisual systems for performance and installation. His work spans technical production, visual art, and custom instrument design, supporting large-scale immersive projects. He has collaborated with artists including Aphex Twin, Grace Jones, Amon Tobin, and institutions such as Tate Modern and FOLD, focusing on pushing the boundaries of audiovisual performance through technology.

name: Custom Fibre Optics Ltd
bio: Custom Fibre Optics Ltd creates immersive light installations inspired by natural forms and systems, using fiber optic lighting to evoke mycelium networks, plant life, and flowing water. Working intuitively with each environment, they design installations that feel organically connected to the spaces they inhabit, from forest floors and gardens to public events and gathering places. Their work transforms ordinary settings into magical experiences that inspire wonder, curiosity, and reflection. Through light, they encourage audiences to notice overlooked beauty and foster deeper connections with the natural world and one another.

name: Damian Grey
title: Owner
bio: Damian Grey is the founder of FilmStory, a Cincinnati-based story development company built for mission-driven storytellers — the ones stuck in the gig-to-gig grind, carrying the doubt alone, ready to stop being vendors for hire and lead with the stories only they can tell. He hosts the StoryFirst podcast and leads a cohort for storytellers ready to step out of isolation.

name: Dan Brown
title: Chief Services Officer
bio:
As Chief Services Officer at JumpStart, Dan Brown leads the organization’s services strategy and execution, helping ensure founders and small business owners across Ohio receive meaningful, high-quality support that drives growth and long-term impact.

Since joining JumpStart in 2023 as an Entrepreneur-in-Residence, Dan has played a key role in expanding the organization’s entrepreneurial support efforts, most notably through leading JumpStart’s growth into Stark County as Director of Entrepreneurial Services. In that role, he helped establish and strengthen relationships across the region’s economic development and entrepreneurial ecosystem, launched collaborative programming, and built strategic partnerships to support entrepreneurs and small businesses throughout the Stark County region.

Before joining JumpStart, Dan co-founded Rust Belt Riders and Tilth Soil, worker-owned social enterprises in Cleveland focused on food waste upcycling and advancing the circular economy. A graduate of JumpStart’s first-ever Impact Program Cohort, his leadership and community impact have earned him recognition as an Echoing Green Global Climate Fellow, an Environmental Leadership Program National Fellow, and Sustainability Advisor on Mayor Bibb’s transition team. He also serves as Board Chair of the Forest City Food Collective, a non-profit organization dedicated to food systems resilience. Prior to launching Rust Belt Riders, Dan held roles with Ohio State University Extension, Cleveland Neighborhood Progress, LAND Studio, and Saint Martin de Porres High School.

Dan is a graduate of DePaul University, where he studied Ethics and Community Service Studies.

name: Daniel Immerwahr
title: Bergen Evans Professor in the Humanities at Northwestern University
bio: Daniel Immerwahr is Bergen Evans Professor in the Humanities at Northwestern University, where he teaches both United States and global history. He is a contributing writer at The New Yorker, and has written two award-winning books, Thinking Small (Harvard, 2015) and the New York Times bestselling How to Hide an Empire (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2019), which has been translated into nine languages. Immerwahr’s writing has appeared in the New York Times, The Atlantic, Harper’s, The New Republic, The Guardian, the New York Review of Books, The Nation, Foreign Policy, and Slate. He lives in Rogers Park, Chicago.

Earlier, Dan co-founded Chartio, a Y Combinator-backed (S10) startup in data visualization, and worked on CrunchBase at TechCrunch. He’s from Washington, DC, and graduated from Yale.

name: Daniel Rossa
bio: Daniel Rossa is a German media artist whose practice operates at the intersection of digital and physical space, creating immersive audiovisual works that dissolve the boundaries between the two and invite new forms of environmental perception. Trained at Bauhaus University Weimar, Rossa draws on an interdisciplinary background in media art, technology, and science to transform architectural structures into dynamic canvases of light, motion, and narrative. His award-winning project, 555 Kubik, reimagined a museum façade as a living, dreamlike entity, using projection mapping and optical illusion to explore the idea of architecture reflecting on itself. By centering each work on the unique qualities of its site, Rossa uses light and imagery to engage buildings as active participants in storytelling, revealing the tension between physical structure and ephemeral intervention.

name: Daniel Shields
bio: Daniel Shields is a Kentucky-based installation artist currently living outside of Cincinnati, Ohio who has used soft yarn to create immersive pieces that cover or enclose large outdoor areas since 2014, but who has only taken art seriously since 2019. Typically, his creations are, at their core, public art which manipulates innate perception of well-known locations in largely unconscious ways by segmenting and dividing 3D space with simple, sparse lines. Most installations use fluorescent acrylic yarn with UV light and UV lasers to create vibrant effects that trick the senses. Some woven installations are visitor-created, where yarn balls are provided and anyone can add their own elements, creating a truly democratic experience where signs read “please touch the art.” Like people and the relationships between them, yarn is seemingly fragile but can be stretched thin and made to endure a tremendous amount of stress without breaking – but there is a limit to everything, and strength in numbers.

bio: Darrin Murriner is the Cofounder and CEO of Cloverleaf.me - the first to market AI coaching technology that brings real-time, personalized coaching in the tools employees use everyday (calendar, email & Slack / Teams). The result is better collaboration, improved employee relationships and a more engaged workforce. Prior to starting Cloverleaf, Darrin had a 15 year corporate career that spanned Munich Re, Arthur Andersen and Fifth Third Bank. Darrin is also the author of Corporate Bravery and Thrive, books focused on building organizational cultures that thrive in the face of change and uncertainty.

name: Dave Hutten
title: Entrepreneur in Residence
bio: Dave Hutten is an entrepreneur and product leader with 25 years of experience building companies across media, digital health and early-stage innovation. He is currently Entrepreneur in Residence at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center within the Innovation Ventures group, where he works with clinicians and researchers to turn promising technologies into investable, market-ready ventures. Dave has spent his career on both sides of the table. He was employee #1 and ultimately VP of Product at Hugo Health, where he helped raise close to $6 million and scale the company from concept to a 40-person team serving Mayo Clinic, Yale, the FDA, Medtronic and Johnson & Johnson. He founded and led Sequel Media, a medical content production company, and later served as an executive in residence at CincyTech, working inside a venture fund to support Cincinnati Children's spinouts. Earlier in his career, before moving into health tech, he was an executive producer at a WPP digital agency in New York, leading global campaigns for Microsoft and InterContinental Hotels Group. Dave is a graduate of DePaul University and advises digital-health startups on product, positioning and fundraising.

name: Dave Theus
title: Entrepreneur in Residence
bio:
Dave Theus is a serial founder and C-suite executive with more than 25 years of leadership across technology driven sectors, including healthcare innovation, artificial intelligence, SaaS, PropTech, InsurTech, and TravelTech. Co-founded and scaled multiple venture-backed companies — raising over $65M in institutional and strategic capital, building organizations of 100+ employees, and guiding businesses from concept through launch, revenue growth, and acquisition. A hands-on operator and trusted advisor to boards, investors, and Fortune 500 partners, with a proven record of translating emerging technology into commercially successful products across B2C, B2B, and B2B2C channels. Currently Executive in Residence at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center, advancing healthcare and research ventures toward real-world impact. Previously, Dave founded and led product, technology, and growth initiatives at several ventures, including:

• Fixle – CEO & Founder of a PropTech platform he spun-out of American Family Insurance.

• Roamie – CTO & Co-Founder of a personalized travel platform developed alongside AAA.

• HOMEE, Inc. – Founder, CTO, CRO, and Director, a PropTech and InsurTech platform, where he drove product, sales, and marketing strategies to fuel rapid growth.

• inno360, Inc. – Chief Product Officer & VP of Technology, where he pioneered enterprise innovation management solutions leveraging IBM Watson AI/ML technologies. Dave is a named inventor on U.S. and international patent filings across three ventures - HOMEE family (U.S., PCT, European, Canadian), an inno360 filing (2011), and two pending Cincinnati Children's applications (2025, 2026). He began his career as an Engineering Analyst in GE’s Technical Leadership Program.. Dave holds a Bachelor’s in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Dayton and a Master of Engineering in Structural Engineering from the University of Cincinnati. His work has been recognized with multiple awards, including CIO Review’s 20 Most Promising Insurance Tech Solution Providers (2020) and Forbes’ Top 10 America’s Best Startup Employers. Passionate about leveraging technology to solve complex, real-world challenges, Dave’s career reflects a consistent commitment to entrepreneurship, innovation, transformation, and creating positive change at scale.

Our specialty is in offering complete motion graphic solutions for a variety of media platforms, such as projection mapping, immersive art, 3D screen, concert, infographic and product launch. To develop visually appealing audience experiences, DecideKit combines passion and competence in data-driven design.

Denise Dunlap Co-Founder and Managing Partner Loon Creek Capital Group Sage Growth Capital denise@looncreekcapital.com denise@sagegrowthcapital.com www.linkedin.com/in/denisedunlap55 Denise brings a rare combination of operator experience, investment acumen, and community leadership to everything she does. Her career spans founding and running companies, mentoring entrepreneurs, and shaping the ecosystems that help them thrive. Earlier roles include CEO of an IT services company and Director of Boise State University’s business incubator. She has been an active angel investor and a recognized leader in the angel investment community since 2008.

Denise co-founded Loon Creek Capital Group in 2010, building it into a trusted resource that provides consulting and administrative services to angel investors across the country. In 2019, she co-founded Sage Growth Capital, a fund dedicated to companies that need growth capital but aren’t a fit for traditional bank or equity financing. She serves as CEO/Managing Partner of both organizations. In 2025, Denise was appointed President of the COBE Advisory Council at Boise State University, where she helps guide the College of Business and Economics in developing the next generation of entrepreneurs and business leaders.

Denise holds a BBA from Boise State University, a first-degree black belt in Shaolin Kung Fu, and is a certified Wrangler/Packer. She collects hobbies the way others collect frequent flyer miles! A few of her interests include golf, growing vegetables, classic cars, riding horses/motorcycles/bicycles, collecting wine, and turning wine bottles into artificial sea glass.

bio: Doug Hardesty is a serial entrepreneur, operator, and AI strategist. He founded Hardesty Operating Group to give founders scaling manufacturing and hard tech companies access to the operator in the room at every scale, taking them from concept to commercial scale through a repeatable operating playbook. As COO of MycoWorks, he took a first-of-kind (FOAK) technology from concept to a greenfield commercial manufacturing facility and global supply chain spanning the U.S. and Europe, leading a company that raised more than $350M and reached a $500M valuation at commercial scale. At Ernst & Young, he led supply chain reinvention work across global industrial, life sciences, and consumer products companies, leading 10+ plant builds and major expansions representing more than $5 billion in capital investment. He started his career at Procter & Gamble, where he built the company's first external manufacturing platform and holds 8 U.S. and international patents. He's holds a Juris Doctor, MBA and cerificate in AI strategy from MIT Sloan.

name: Drew Merritt
bio: Drew Merritt is an American painter and muralist known for his striking realism and his ability to merge classical aesthetics with contemporary urban environments. Beginning his career nearly three decades ago as a graffiti writer in New Mexico, he has since created monumental murals across the United States and internationally, working with brands and organizations such as Tesla, Adidas, UFC, Converse, and Virgin Hotels. His work often juxtaposes Renaissance-inspired portraiture with modern settings, exploring themes of empathy, vulnerability, and time while translating fine art realism to architectural scale through spray paint and latex. Alongside his mural practice, he maintains a fine art studio practice in oil painting, exhibiting work in galleries worldwide and bridging the worlds of street art, fine art, and cultural storytelling.

name: Dulk
bio: Spanish artist Antonio Segura, Dulk, is one of the most important names in Spanish painting of the moment internationally. His body of work begins to form in urban art and mural painting to which he remains closely linked today along with study work, but does not stop there. He continues to research and constantly create new forms of expression through different media, drawing, sculpture or photography among others. Dulk’s paintings are the immediate byproduct of his travels into remote areas and his memories of a natural wonder and wildlife. He has witnessed first hand both the beauty of these landscapes and the terrible collapse that is creeping over them like a fatal tide. By painting something beautiful he asks audiences to gather the strength to look away from art and toward nature, as painful as that may be. With a strong ecological conviction to defend ecosystems and the most vulnerable species, his work invites the viewer to be part of a unique imaginarium, full of energy and with a special sensitivity to color. A dream world with animals and natural spaces that tells personal, universal and unique stories.

name: Elijah Howe
title: Photographer
bio: Elijah Howe is a photographer who currently lives and works in Felton, CA. His work focuses on the fragmentary nature of photography and people’s relationships with one another, as well as their relationship with the land. Howe’s work explores quiet transitionary spaces in the landscape and the unsettling melancholy of the human condition.

name: Elizabeth Leitzell
title: Photographer and Short Filmmaker
bio: Elizabeth Leitzell is a photographer, short-film maker, and editor based in the Greater Philadelphia Area. On most days, you’ll find her working on collaborations with visual artists, musicians, authors, start-ups, and non-profit institutions in the arts, social services, and sciences. She believes in using the power of image-based narratives for social change. Through a free exploration of color, composition, listening, and emotion, Leitzell hopes her work can support building new systems of cooperation, reconciliation, and reorganization. Her style lends itself to the past in its representation of ancient symbols, patterns and colour schemes , while voicing an intuitively current aesthetic that resonates and seeks to redefine emotional iconography. She has immersed herself in the creative world, working alongside established artists, as well as furthering her own practice, taking part in shows and creating murals in both South Africa and internationally.

name: Everything Good Studio
bio: Everything Good Studio is a Brooklyn-based multidisciplinary art and design collaboration between Rachel Ciavarella and Jack Kalish, focused on the creative use of emerging technologies. Their practice centers on light as a dynamic and immersive medium, using tools such as digital LEDs and projection to create kinetic, participatory environments that engage audiences directly. They believe art is completed through audience interaction and design their work to challenge perception, inviting viewers to experience the world with a sense of childlike openness and imagination. Through public art commissions and international exhibitions across the United States, Europe, and Asia, the studio creates immersive experiences that explore light as a universal and emotionally resonant force.

name: Felix Frank
bio: This German digital artist creates mapping and light installations that transform architectural spaces into immersive visual environments. Born in Munich in the late 1970s and educated in Fine Arts in Paris and Motion Design in Barcelona, their practice is shaped by early influences from Waldorf education and the graffiti and hip-hop culture of the 1990s, which first sparked a drive to reshape public space through visual intervention. Today, they work with projection mapping and large-scale light installations, replacing spray paint with projected “light paintings” while maintaining a focus on nighttime urban environments. Their work combines detailed animation with carefully tuned sound design, often incorporating specific frequencies, to create immersive experiences that aim to shift perception and evoke states of harmony and presence.

name: Filip Roca
bio: This media artist works at the intersection of light, architecture, and motion, creating projection mapping and live generative visuals that transform facades into dynamic visual systems. Based between Barcelona and Lisbon, their practice evolved from over a decade in animation, motion graphics, and art direction into large-scale architectural light works presented internationally at festivals and institutions including Fête des Lumières, iMapp, Noor Riyadh, Tokyo Lights, and the Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza. Treating architecture as an instrument, they use light not as decoration but as structural force, revealing hidden geometries, flow fields, and latent tensions within built forms. Their process combines site data, parametric systems, and tightly synchronized audiovisual composition to create precise, high-contrast transformations that explore themes of structure, transformation, and perception at city scale.

name: Freddy Mac
title: On Air Talent
bio:
Hey! I’m Freddy Mac. A dad, shoe addict, brunch enthusiast, and your friend on the radio.

I grew up on the East Coast, and as of 6 years ago, Cincinnati is my home. The biggest, coolest thing about me? I’m a dad, and I’ve been wrapped around those tiny human fingers since before he was born.

I’m one of those people who somehow always knew radio was “it.” Maybe it was doing the morning announcements in 5th grade… maybe it was talking way too much in class, and getting in trouble. Either way, now I get to hang with you every day, and I’m pretty sure I’ve got the best job in the world!

When I’m not on the air, you’ll probably find me: • DJ'ing a wedding around town • hunting for new pizza and wing spots or enjoying brunch • adding another pair of Nikes to my collection • binge-watching something way past bedtime • playing drums at church (started at age 2. You'll have ask my parents how they survived) • soaking up as much family time with my son, Cam I love meeting new people and connecting beyond the radio airwaves

name: Gee Horton
bio: Gee Horton (/dʒi ˈhɔːrtən/) is an American contemporary artist based in Cincinnati, Ohio. He is recognized for his graphite and charcoal portraiture, as well as mixed-media works that address themes of identity, memory, and emotional experience. Horton's practice often integrates photorealistic drawing with archival materials and installation, focusing on aspects of Black adolescence and masculinity.

name: GERA 1
bio: This artist’s journey began in 2009 with graffiti in their hometown, later expanding into formal training in painting, drawing, and fine arts studies beginning in 2015. After three years of academic exploration in printmaking, painting, and photography, they began traveling and creating murals across European festivals, eventually holding their first solo exhibition in San Francisco in 2023. Now based in Athens, Greece, their practice draws heavily from photography as a source of inspiration, using captured textures, reflections, and human presence as the foundation for layered compositions. Through painting and mixed-media experimentation across surfaces such as canvas, aluminum composite, and plexiglass, they distort and reconfigure imagery to create vibrant visual worlds where color drives movement, emotion, and form.

name: Grayson Stalvey
title: Founder
bio: Grayson Stalvey is the founder of Aegis Runway Systems, where he helps early-stage founders improve financial visibility, understand burn rate and runway, and make better decisions with limited capital. He is a Coast Guard veteran, entrepreneur, MBA, and Fortune 50 operations leader with more than 20 years of experience in operations, cost management, procurement, decision-making, and resource allocation. Grayson has also coached individuals and businesses on financial management and budgeting topics for more than six years.

Greg Pipkins is an entrepreneur, strategist, and organizing member of FoundHouse, where he leads sales strategy, relationship development, and strategic partnerships. He is also the CEO and co-founder of Kept House and serves as Third Vice President of the North Avondale Neighborhood Association.

A husband, father, son, and friend, Greg’s work is grounded in relationships, service, and creating meaningful opportunities for people and communities. At FoundHouse, he helps connect each client’s immediate challenges with custom software, AI and workflow automation, and ongoing technology support that strengthens their long-term capacity. FoundHouse combines the rigor and results of a large technology firm with the responsiveness and agility of a small business—helping clients become more capable, confident, and ready to scale revenue.

bio: Heesoo Kwon is a multimedia artist and educator based in San Francisco and Los Angeles. Having initiated the autobiographical feminist religion and speculative universe Leymusoom in 2017, she has exhibited internationally for nearly a decade. Kwon’s work is held in the permanent collections of the Cantor Arts Center at Stanford University, KADIST, Huis Marseille, and the University of California Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art, and has been covered by Hyperallergic, Artforum, Rhizome, the Brooklyn Rail, and e-flux, among others. name: Holly Shoemaker
title: Director of Brand Strategy
bio:
With 28 years of experience, Holly has become a trusted authority in naming, brand strategy, and creating brand identities for Fortune 100 companies. She has played a pivotal role in building some of the most iconic brands in the world, earning her reputation as a visionary in the field.

Holly’s approach to brand building is rooted in her belief that creativity thrives in a positive, collaborative environment. By fostering open, honest communication, she has established strong, enduring relationships with teams and clients alike. Known for her passion and ability to inspire, Holly leads with a focus on innovation and an energy that makes the creative process as enjoyable as it is impactful. Her philosophy is clear: positivity fuels creativity, and when channeled effectively, it leads to extraordinary results.

name: Ilana Habib
title: Principal
bio: Ilana Habib is Principal at Cintrifuse Capital, a venture fund and innovation hub backing early-stage founders and strengthening the Cincinnati startup ecosystem. She’s spent her career in and around the entrepreneurial ecosystem and loves rolling up her sleeves to support founders and operators. She’s also an avid traveller, taking her camera with her to capture some of the most interesting places on earth.

name: illumaphonium
bio: This family-led creative team specializes in the design, fabrication, installation, and maintenance of large-scale interactive light art installations around the world. Drawing on expertise in design, engineering, computer science, creative therapies, music, and a proudly neurodiverse perspective, the team creates immersive works that blur the boundaries between art, entertainment, and participation. Their installations prioritize accessibility and human connection, inviting people of all ages and backgrounds to engage through intuitive, collaborative experiences that require no instruction or prior knowledge. Rooted in a belief that art should bring people together, their work fosters creativity, equality, wonder, and shared moments of discovery in public spaces.

name: Inka Kendzia
bio: Inka Kendzia is an award-winning interdisciplinary artist, VJ, and director who uses light, projection, and emerging technologies to explore humanity’s connection to nature and shared experience. Working across VR, AI, and generative visuals, she creates immersive works designed to encourage reflection and collective engagement. As a motion design director and live visual artist, she has produced work for projects including The Beatles: Eight Days a Week and Luciano Pavarotti documentaries, and has directed performances for artists such as Black Coffee, Seal, and Ibeyi. Her collaborations span international festivals, theatres, and institutions, including the Smithsonian Museum of African Art and Everard Read Gallery, as well as award-winning public installations like AD PACEM presented at BLINK Cincinnati.

He has also held strategic and operational leadership roles at Gorilla Glue, Scripps, and Twitter.

He specializes in MA3 lighting programming and Disguise d3 media server programming. His experience spans a wide range of production environments, including house-of-worship production, systems integration, rental warehouse operations, music festivals and theatre. Most recently, he has worked with touring artists including CAIN and Charli XCX. Outside of his studies, Jack works locally as a contract lighting director with Crossroads Church and is employed by COUR Design in Nashville, Tennessee.

Past CCM credits include: Lighting Designer for "Love Letter" (Poiesis Quartet) and Moveable Feast: Illuminate (CCM Philharmonia). Associate Designer for Student Choreographers' Showcase 2025. name: Jaimin Gandhi
title: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer
bio: Jaimin Gandhi is Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer at Redi Health, where he oversees Product, Engineering, Design, and Implementation. His work focuses on modernizing how pharmaceutical patient support programs operate by connecting fragmented vendor ecosystems into unified, patient-centric platforms. He enables faster access to therapy by simplifying enrollment, reducing operational friction, and embedding automated intelligence into complex healthcare workflows. Jaimin brings a systems-level perspective to building compliant, scalable infrastructure that improves patient outcomes and patient support program performance.

name: Jake Rouse
title: Co-Founder & CEO
bio: Jake Rouse is a passionate entrepreneur who believes in the power of food and beverage to bring people together. As Co-Founder and CEO of Braxton Brewing Company, he’s helped shape one of the Midwest’s most innovative breweries - creating vibrant, community-focused taprooms and pushing the boundaries of beer and beverage manufacturing. In 2021, Jake founded Hit Seekers, a next-generation sports card retail and live streaming company. Fueled by authenticity and entertainment, it quickly became a national presence and was named Cincinnati’s fastest-growing company in 2024. A 40 Under 40 honoree, Jake is driven by a deep belief in connection—whether through craft beer, collectibles, or community events—because the best things in life are meant to be shared.

name: James Bullough
bio: James Bullough is an American-born artist living and working in Berlin, Germany, known for his large-scale murals and studio paintings that merge realistic portraiture with graphic distortion and abstraction. His practice is shaped by a combination of influences, including the raw energy of urban graffiti he encountered growing up in Washington, D.C., and the disciplined study of Old Master oil painting techniques. By combining these contrasting approaches, he creates visually striking works that balance technical precision with expressive disruption. His murals and studio works have been exhibited internationally in galleries, museums, and art fairs, and can be found on landmark walls across Europe, the Americas, and beyond.

name: Jeff Harris
title: Chef, Owner
bio:
Four-time James Beard-nominated Chef Jeffrey Harris has called Cincinnati home since 2005, when the New Orleans native relocated to the Queen City following Hurricane Katrina. After working his way through some of Cincinnati’s top restaurants, Chef Jeff launched his first concept, Jimmie Lou’s, in 2021 as an ode to his beloved grandmother. In 2022, he opened Nolia Kitchen in Over-the-Rhine, bringing an inventive and deeply personal approach to Southern cuisine that quickly earned local and national recognition.

As his profile has grown, Chef Jeff has used his platform to invest back into the city and hospitality community that embraced him. Beyond the kitchen, he is an entrepreneur, mentor, connector, and community builder committed to creating opportunities for culinary professionals and strengthening Cincinnati’s food ecosystem. In 2024, he founded Chef & Coffee, a gathering designed to bring chefs and chef-adjacent professionals together to connect, collaborate, and support one another.

title: Brewer, Director of Partnerships
bio: Since joining the Samuel Adams Boston Brewery in 2001, Jennifer Glanville has played an integral role in the research and development of experimental Samuel Adams brews, honing her craft at the renowned Doemens Brewing Academy in Germany. Passionate about traditional and lost beer styles, as well as barrel-aged and extreme beers such as Samuel Adams Utopias and Kosmic Mother Funk, Jennifer has helped push the boundaries of craft brewing. Named one of Fast Company’s “Most Creative People in Business” and an award-winning cookbook author, she now serves as Director of Partnerships at The Boston Beer Company, where she leads the company’s flagship philanthropy initiative, Brewing the American Dream, supports small business owners and breweries nationwide, and cultivates strategic collaborations and research efforts across the brewing and cider industries to champion the integrity and future of craft.

name: Jérémie Bellot
bio: Jérémie Bellot is a French architect and visual artist whose practice bridges architecture, digital art, and large-scale projection mapping. Trained in both cinema and architecture, he became a state-certified architect before dedicating himself fully to artistic practice in 2010, co-founding AV-Exciters and later leading AV Extended as artistic director. His work focuses on architectural video mapping and immersive light installations, often created in collaboration with musicians and designers for major cultural events and monuments worldwide. He has served as curator and creative director for projects such as the Constellations de Metz festival and the Château de Beaugency digital art center, and has received multiple awards including the Trophée des Lumières and Cannes Heavent Awards for landmark projection works on sites such as Place Stanislas in Nancy and the Basilica of Zaragoza.

name: jeremy jarrett
title: President & CEO
bio: Jeremy Jarrett is CEO of Kinetic Vision, a Cincinnati-based technology and product development company specializing in digital transformation, advanced manufacturing, AI, simulation, and automation. With extensive experience helping organizations adopt emerging technologies, Jeremy brings a practical perspective on the evolution of robotics and automation and how these tools are transforming the factory floor.

name: Jérémy Oury
bio: Jérémy Oury is a French digital artist and sound designer whose work explores perception, space, and light through immersive audiovisual environments. With a background in sound design for theatre and architectural acoustics, he creates fulldome films, video mapping works, and light installations that investigate the relationship between reality, technology, and consciousness. His practice, presented internationally at festivals and venues such as MUTEK MX, Mapping Festival, ISEA, FILE, Artechouse, and the Paris Planetarium, blends algorithmic visuals and generative soundscapes to construct sensory environments where order and chaos coexist. Through these immersive systems, Oury invites viewers into contemplative experiences that blur the boundaries between digital space and inner perception.

name: Jill Morenz

Jill has created three businesses in her career and leverages those insights as the President and Chief Executive Officer of Aviatra, as she works with women entrepreneurs to set them up for business success.

name: Jim Tucker and Frank Young
bio:
Frank D. Young

Frank D. Young is an American fine art photographer whose portraits treat their subjects as living documents of their existence. Though he has always had a camera in his hands, he began his journey as an artist in 2008, building a practice rooted in analog processes and equipment while moving fluidly between film and digital capture. Since 2012, he has documented the Black residents of Cincinnati's Over-the-Rhine, a neighborhood reshaped by economic revitalization and gentrification, creating a portrait record of a community in the midst of change. His clients include the Cincinnati Regional Chamber, the World Affairs Council of America, 1001 Colors, Duke Energy, Mortar, 3CDC, and The City Flea. Drawing on influences from Gordon Parks and Richard Avedon to Carrie Mae Weems, Jamel Shabazz, and Spike Lee, his work bridges documentary tradition and fine art portraiture, framing everyday people with the dignity and permanence of the historical record.

Jim Tucker

Jim Tucker is a British-born artist and educator whose passion is to use art to build community through collaboration and education. Since leaving England in 2007, he traveled extensively before settling in Cincinnati in 2021, carrying with him a belief in "eating what the locals eat," a phrase that signifies reverence and respect for the culture of every new place. He interprets his surroundings through site-specific automatic painting, generating imagery and characters that he contrasts with work inspired by historical and contemporary photography of the area. Since moving to Cincinnati, he has produced and painted over twenty murals, many in partnership with 1001 Colors and now recognized as city landmarks, and collaborated with institutions including the Cincinnati Art Museum, the Marketer Collaborative, and several Big Tech companies. Across a combined career of more than twenty years, his work bridges fine art, murals, and community building.

The Collaboration

Jim and Frank have been working together for several years, with Jim licensing Frank's photographs as references in his paintings and installations. BLINK 2026 marks the first time the two are coming together for a unique hybrid mural, combining a wheat paste of Frank's photography against Jim's painted interpretation of the mural's location.

name: Jimmy Sauter
title: Growth and Partnerships Manager
bio: Jimmy Sauter works on growth and partnerships at Pay Theory, a Cincinnati payments startup, where he helps with go-to-market, outbound, and brand. He started out learning most of it on the job. He mentors students through a fellows program and spoke at StartupCincy Week in 2025.

title: Foresight Researcher

bio: Mechanical Engineering student at University of Cincinnati. Strategic Advisor at Bearcat Ventures, deploying $200K+ from UC's $1M student fund. Futures Foresight Researcher at NEXT Innovation Scholars, exploring how the choices we make today shape the landscape of tomorrow.

name: Joe Rohan
title: Director of Startup Programs
bio: Joe Rohan is the Director of Startup Programs at BRITE Energy Innovators. In his role, Joe helps early-stage startups build the foundation needed to build a business from the ground up, launch successful fundraising rounds, and enter the market.

name: John Bentley
title: Fractional CTO
bio: John Bentley II is the founder of Product Journey Group, where he works with founders on the decision in front of them — what to build, what to fix, what to stop — before any of it becomes code. A practitioner for 35 years, he spent the last eight as founder and CTO/CPO of 10XTS, building and shipping the same decisions he now helps founders make. He runs AI and agents across definition, development, and operations under accountable human authority rather than in place of it. Through the Product Journey — Define → Build → Launch — he helps early-stage founders cut decision waste and reach an MVP that's easier to launch, operate, and evolve, and helps scaling teams get a live product back under control. He takes fractional CTO engagements where a bounded leadership mandate is the right answer.

name: John Hurley
title: leads marketing
bio:
John Hurley leads marketing at Notion, where he runs product marketing, demand, content, and regional go-to-market as the company scales.

Before Notion, he built product marketing at Amplitude through its growth from $50 million to $250 million ARR and its IPO. He started even earlier as a first go-to-market hire at Radius, joining pre-seed and staying through acquisition.

He has spent fifteen years in the middle of product and go-to-market, usually sitting next to founders.

name: John Yuksel
title: Co-Founder & CEO
bio: John Yuksel is the co-founder and CEO of Beltways, an American OEM that designs, builds, operates, and maintains the world's only accelerators.

name: Jon Thompson
title: Founder/Writer/Director
bio: Jon Thompson is a Cincinnati-based filmmaker, award-winning marketer and entrepreneur with more than 15 years of experience building audiences and creating culture-driven work across entertainment, technology and some of the world’s biggest brands. He is the creator and director of Coworking, a Cincinnati-produced vertical comedy series exploring the personalities, relationships and absurdities of modern work. The series brings together local actors, creators, startups and brands while experimenting with new ways to tell and distribute scripted stories for mobile audiences. Before focusing on filmmaking, Jon built a career in social media and digital strategy, working with brands and organizations including Snapchat, Kroger, Jordan Brand, M&M's and the USTA/US Open. His work has spanned social strategy, emerging technology, influencer marketing, experiential activations and audience development. Today, Jon is focused on the intersection of storytelling, entrepreneurship and emerging, helping build Cincinnati into a place where creators can experiment with what entertainment looks like next.

name: Jonas Denzel
bio: Jonas Denzel (*1990) is a filmmaker and visual artist with a focus on projection mapping, video installation, and documentary film. In 2016, he received a Fulbright Scholarship and studied Film and Media Art at Temple University in Philadelphia. In 2018, Denzel completed his master’s degree in “Time-based Media” with distinction. Commissioned works for public, urban spaces in Leipzig, Chicago and Bucharest among others, followed. In 2021 he won the international video competition IMAPP in Bucharest. As an artist and drummer Jonas‘ goal is to make the audience become part of projections and their locations. He uses rhythms and patterns to create interactive projections. The influence of drums and percussions play an important role in his work.

name: Jordanne Renner
title: Multidisciplinary Artist
bio: Jordanne Renner is a multidisciplinary portrait artist that primarily works within large format film photography, figurative sculpture, mixed media painting, public art, and installation. The notion of self, culture of place, the body and landscape, what we eat, and the psychology of memory are recurring topics of investigation in her work, as well as the idea of the photograph as an object. Split between the Midwest and the East Coast, Renner divides her time between studio practice, community endeavors, and teaching. She is a member of the National League of American Pen Women and the Society for Photographic Education, and is the Creative Wild of Gallery Palindroma & the ArtLab located in the Lower Hudson Valley.

name: Jordon Kuhn
title: Launch Program Manager
bio: I have worked in the restaurant and hospitality industry for more than 20 years, with experience spanning restaurant operations, culinary training, workforce development, and food business support. At Findlay Market, I served as the chef and program manager for Mighty Good, a hospitality workforce training program focused on preparing individuals for careers in the food industry. For the past three years, I have focused on supporting startup and growing food businesses at Findlay Market through educational courses, one-on-one advising, and connections to industry professionals and resources. My work combines hands-on restaurant experience with business development and mentorship to help food entrepreneurs build stronger, more sustainable businesses.

name: Joseph Vitone
title: Photographer
bio: Joe Vitone is a documentary fine art photographer and educator. His work consists of large format portraiture and landscape in the United States, as well as panoramic and other views examining cultures abroad. He is Professor of Photocommunications at St. Edward’s University in Austin, TX, where he teaches both traditional and digital photography along with electronic media. He has received a National Endowment for the Arts Fellowship in Photography and was a Fulbright scholar in Costa Rica, as well as a Fulbright Specialist in the Apulia region of southern Italy. In Italy, Vitone’s work centered around small-scale, family-based agriculture and the evidence of place and culture in the urban area. In addition to presentations given in the United States, he has lectured on his photography in Australia, China, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Japan, Malaysia, Thailand, and Vietnam. His work has been exhibited at a number of venues including solo exhibitions at the Hungarian Museum of Photography, Kecskemét, Hungary; the Akron Art Museum, OH; and the Instituto Cultural Peruano Norteamericano, Lima, Peru. His work is held in a number of collections including the Cleveland Museum of Art, OH; the Center for Creative Photography at the University of Arizona, Tucson; the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, TX; the Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest, Hungary; and the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History, Washington, D.C. (Photo credit: Dylan Vitone)

name: Joshua Berg
title: Artist
bio: Joshua Berg is a photographer based in Covington, KY, at the confluence of the Ohio and Licking Rivers. Bound by the rhythms of two rivers, his work centers on the idea of home and the experience of living and growing up in the Midwest. His books and photographs explore the impossibility of untethering the body from place, and the endless dialogue of unraveling the actual. (Photo Credit: Brian Pfaff)

name: JP Jackson + Brian Havener
bio: Architects by trade, JP Jackson and Brian Havener began their friendship and collaboration while at the University of Cincinnati's College of Design, Architecture, Art & Planning. Although separate paths led them to settle in Nashville and Seattle respectively, JP and Brian's shared work continues through a mutual appreciation for immersive experiences that are shaped by craft and latent material qualities. Their projects often re-imagine the mundane, transforming conventional objects into unexpected spatial encounters. Lighting plays a constant and formative role in amplifying the underlying intention of each work.

name: Juan Fuentes
bio: After studying architecture, he specialized in lighting and digital manufacturing. His multidisciplinary training allows him to fully develop his designs. Juan Fuentes' artistic line is based on perception and geometry, evoking immersive sensations and experiences in the audience, blurring the line between the real and the virtual. He works on his projects within biomimicry, using nature as a source of inspiration. In recent years, he has exhibited in Light Art exhibitions around the world, including Madrid, Sydney, Singapore, Vancouver, Brussels, London, Stockholm. In 2021, he received the 40under40 award as one of the top 40 lighting designers in the world.

name: Julia Dewey
title: Chief Partnerships Officer
bio:
As Chief Partnerships Officer at Rev1 Ventures, Julia Dewey leads marketing and strategic collaboration with private and public sector funding partners, including corporates, research institutions, and economic development entities. Rev1 is a Midwest venture studio that partners with innovators in SaaS/AI, deep tech, and life sciences, helping startups validate markets, gain traction, and become venture ready.

Julia's partnerships team works with enterprises to innovate through Rev1's startup studio framework, helping to source, vet, engage, and invest in market-leading technologies. Prior to Rev1 Ventures, Julia played instrumental roles in scaling and shaping several notable organizations. At CoverMyMeds, she helped navigate the company through a billion-dollar acquisition, expanding market reach through the development of health plan and payer partnerships. She also held key positions at CAS, where she led commercial and academic partnerships that facilitated the exchange of scientific knowledge and drove innovation across various sectors.

She holds a Bachelor of Science in Biology and a Master's in Public Health, both from The Ohio State University. This foundation gives her a unique perspective, blending scientific rigor with a comprehensive understanding of healthcare dynamics and their impact on entrepreneurial ecosystems.
