title: Sr. Manager of Consumer Insights
bio: Julie Messer is Sr. Manager of Consumer Insights at Boston Beer Company, where she leads the Consumer Insights team and helps shape brand, innovation, and marketing strategy across the company's portfolio. She is responsible for consumer research, brand health tracking, and translating consumer understanding into actionable business decisions. Julie has extensive experience in CPG insights and is passionate about helping teams use consumer-centric thinking to drive growth, innovation, and stronger brand connections.

name: Julie Renée Jones
title: Artist
bio:
Julie Renée Jones is a photographic-based artist and educator currently living in Dayton, OH. Her work explores autobiographical narratives related to familial myth and matrescence, using the camera as a tool to reveal magic residing within the everyday and memory as a medium for approaching the unknown.

Her work has been exhibited extensively across the United States and internationally, and has been published in National Geographic and the British Journal of Photography. A selection of images from her series Hold Still is featured in Eye Mama: Poetic Truths of Home and Motherhood published by teNeues. She is a recipient of numerous awards and grants in support of her work, including two Ohio Arts Council’s Individual Excellence Awards.

name: Justin Boh
bio: Justin Boh (also known as Post Humongous) is a Kentucky-based creative director and immersive artist whose work explores the intersection of technology, storytelling, and community engagement. With over two decades of experience leading projects for brands such as Amazon, Disney, Google, Old Spice, Dell Technologies, and Pixar, he combines strategy and emotional narrative to create impactful visual experiences. His installations use projection mapping and generative media to transform public spaces into interactive environments that respond in real time to audience movement and participation. Through these systems, Boh reframes interactivity as a language of connection, turning viewers into co-creators and fostering shared discovery, play, and collective expression.

name: Kailah Ware
title: Creative Director / Founder
bio: Kailah Ware is an Emmy-nominated filmmaker, creative director, and narrative strategist driven by a commitment to social impact and mission-centered storytelling. As Founder and Creative Director of SunnyBlu Art Agency, she helps nonprofits, public sector partners, and values-led organizations translate complex issues into clear, compelling campaigns that move people to action. Her work spans public health, civic engagement, workforce development, economic mobility, and narrative change, with campaigns reaching millions and earning national and regional recognition. A Wright State University graduate with a background in motion pictures production and studio art, Kailah brings a cinematic, research-informed approach to strategic communications, digital campaigns, and public-facing storytelling.

She currently serves as Program Manager for RedHawk50 at Miami University’s John W. Altman Institute for Entrepreneurship, where she works with alumni entrepreneurs and the broader Miami University entrepreneurship community. Kara also serves as Marketing Director at The Mercantile Library in Cincinnati, leading marketing, membership engagement, programming, and communications for one of the country’s oldest member-supported libraries. Throughout her career, she has worked across marketing, events, entrepreneurship, community building, and brand strategy, with a particular passion for creating memorable experiences and developing programs that help people connect. Her work is driven by a belief that great marketing is about more than promotion. It is about building communities, telling meaningful stories, and creating opportunities for people to engage with organizations in authentic and unexpected ways.

name: Kasumi Art Studios
bio: This artist’s practice blends physical materials with digital and time-based media to create immersive sculptural and cinematic works that explore how movement, sound, and memory shape perception in public space. Their work spans projection mapping, responsive installations, lenticular prints, and large-scale environmental media, often designed to activate architecture and transform how audiences experience built environments. Sound plays a foundational role in their process, informed by a background as a classically trained musician and collaborations with artists such as Grandmaster Flash, DJ Spooky, and Warren Harris (Hanna), as well as custom scores for experimental film and installation projects. With work exhibited internationally—from Carnegie Hall and the Cleveland Museum of Art to major public projection festivals—their practice consistently investigates memory, identity, and transformation through emotionally resonant, symbolically rich audiovisual experiences that invite participation and reflection.

name: Kate Bonansinga
title: Director of the School of Art

name: Katie Stratman
title: Student Venture Analyst
bio: I'm a senior at Northern Kentucky University studying Finance, Entrepreneurship, and Human Resources and I've spent the last year doing something that didn't exist before I showed up. As the first Student Venture Analyst at Norse Ventures, NKU's student-run venture fund, I was handed a blank slate and told to build. So I did. I developed the fund's investment process from the ground up, building a custom deal flow platform using Claude Code, creating the scorecard we used to evaluate our first investment, and leading recruiting efforts to grow awareness of the fund across campus. Being first means there's no playbook. You figure it out, you ask the right questions, and you build something you're proud of. Beyond Norse Ventures, I recently accepted a position with Flamel.ai as an intern, and I'm constantly showing up to events across the Northern Kentucky and Cincinnati startup ecosystem. This region has real momentum, and I want to be part of it. I'm passionate about connecting with founders, capital, and community in a way that moves this ecosystem forward. If you're building something, investing in something, or just love the NKY/Cincy startup scene, let's connect.

name: Katie Thompson
title: Sr. Analyst/Program Manager
bio:
Katie Thompson is a Sr. Analyst and Program Manager at Gotara, an operator-led consulting firm that helps companies grow through business transformation, M&A integration, exit readiness, and scaling the leaders behind the work. Katie partners with Gotara's operators to lead the client work. In addition, she also focuses on the marketing and outreach side—sharpening how the firm shows up in the market, telling the stories behind its impact, and opening doors with the leaders and companies who could benefit from it.

She joined Gotara as a senior-year intern at Miami University and has grown alongside the company ever since. Today, her work spans everything from digital marketing strategy and content to AEO/SEO, outreach, events, and project management. She enjoys being in the middle of a growing company, figuring out how to turn ideas into something tangible, useful, and ultimately tied to business results. She has represented Gotara at conferences and customer meetings.

name: Ke Jyun Wu
bio: Ke Jyun Wu is a Taiwanese media artist whose work exists at the intersection of the virtual and the real, blending engineering, nature, and emotional resonance into immersive digital environments. His practice transforms everyday natural phenomena—such as wind, water, and light—into generative, interactive systems where light, sound, motion, and viewer interaction converge to create subtle sensory experiences. Central to his process is the use of a single poetic sentence as both conceptual anchor and creative constraint, from which he develops digital ecologies that prioritize presence, stillness, and feeling over representation. Through works like his DigiScape series, he invites audiences into reflective spaces that reframe perception and encourage a deeper sensitivity to the world around them.

name: Keep Cincinnati Beautiful
bio: Keep Cincinnati Beautiful is a grassroots nonprofit that has connected people, passion, and place since 1978, fostering community-driven public spaces and environmental stewardship throughout Cincinnati. Since 2009, its team of artists has partnered with neighborhoods, nonprofits, businesses, and volunteers to transform overlooked and neglected spaces into vibrant public art installations. Through this collaborative approach, Keep Cincinnati Beautiful works to reduce blight, increase community pride, promote environmental awareness, and improve quality of life for residents across the city.

name: Kelly Dolan
title: Entrepreneur in Residence
bio: Kelly Dolan is a serial entrepreneur, advisor, and Entrepreneur-in-Residence at Miami University. She has founded and led multiple purpose-driven ventures and brings firsthand experience navigating co-founder relationships, organizational growth, and business transitions.

name: Kelly Kucharczyk
title: Principal Consultant
bio:
Kelly Kucharczyk is a Principal Consultant who partners with startups to help navigate the complexities of medical device development, with a strong passion for developing commercialization strategies that look across regulatory, reimbursement, and clinical to align with the overarching business objective. She serves as a strategic ally helping companies intentionally scale for sustainable growth or position for a successful exit.

With extensive expertise in global market entry and FDA negotiations, Kelly is experienced in building "acquisition-ready" Quality Management Systems (QMS) and Design History Files (DHF). Her leadership background includes serving as a Director at NAMSA, where she guided global teams across Regulatory, Quality, and Medical Writing. Prior to this, Kelly spent nearly a decade at Stryker, driving regulatory strategies for new product development and managing complex M&A activities from initial due diligence through full post-acquisition integration.

Outside of the Medtech world, she is an outdoor enthusiast and avid gardener who can frequently be found foraging for wild foods, experimenting with new recipes in the kitchen, or collaborating on "toddler art" masterpieces.

name: Kelly Shaw
title: Associate Director
bio: Kelly Shaw is the Associate Director of Findlay Kitchen, bringing over 15 years of hospitality experience across a wide range of roles, from line cook, kitchen manager, catering sales, and many others in between. She also has extensive experience in customer service and administrative management, giving her a well rounded perspective on both the operational and people focused sides of the food industry. In her role at Findlay Kitchen, Kelly supports members, oversees day to day operations, and is helping lead Findlay Kitchen into its next phase of growth. Kelly also recently launched her own small pop up food business, Okie Doke, giving her firsthand insight into the challenges and opportunities that come with building a food business.

name: Kemper Sauce Studios
bio: Kemper Sauce Studios is a Cincinnati based engineering and arts collective with an inventive spirit and a whole list of bad ideas. Ultimately, our goal is to bring communities together by providing fun and memorable experiences in the form of large scale light based art installations.

name: Kerry Taft
title: Founder
bio:
Kerry Taft is the expert entrepreneurs call when their business systems are holding them back. She’s the one founders turn to when they’re ready to stop duct-taping systems together and start running a company that works without them.

With over 20 years in the health sciences as an exercise physiologist and former university professor, Kerry brings both analytical rigor and a deeply human-centered approach to every system she builds.

In 2024, she acquired and integrated a digital agency into her growing portfolio, further solidifying her role as a strategic force in the operations space. Founders seek her out when they’re ready to reclaim their time, streamline their backend, and build businesses that run smoothly—and feel better.

notes: Headshot credit: Madeleine Hordinski. Also "Kevin Moore, Ph.D., FotoFocus Artistic Director and Curator" (curator of the Trevor Paglen exhibition).

name: Kia S. Smith
title: Artistic Director, South Chicago Dance Theatre

name: Kimm Lauterbach
title: President & CEO
bio: Kimm Lauterbach REDI Cincinnati President and CEO As President and CEO of REDI Cincinnati since 2018 and a founding member of its leadership team, Kimm engineers economic development strategies to enhance the global competitiveness of the three-state, 15-county Cincinnati region. Following five years as vice president of business development, she transformed the economic landscape, overseeing all aspects of deals for companies locating or expanding in the region. Kimm serves on the board of directors for the Cincinnati USA Regional Chamber, Cincinnati Experience, BE NKY Growth Partnership, the Federal Reserve Southwest Ohio & Northern Kentucky Business Advisory Council, and the University of Cincinnati Research Institute. In 2024, she was honored as a YWCA Career Woman of Achievement. A magna cum laude graduate of Indiana University's MPA program, Kimm focused on nonprofit management and public policy, holding a BA in political science from the University of Dayton. She resides in Mason, Ohio, with her husband, Leo, and enjoys SCUBA diving, live music, Bengal's games, and supporting her two adult daughters' endeavors.

name: Koros Design Studio
bio: This creative practice develops immersive light-based installations that explore the intersection of nature, technology, and human perception. Combining digitally generated designs with experimental materials such as lightweight inflatable fabrics, the team creates walkable environments that encourage both reflection and play. Their work uses light as both a sculptural medium and a metaphor for connection, transforming spaces while inviting audiences to engage with the world in new ways. By blending tactile materials with digital innovation, they create experiences that celebrate the harmony between natural phenomena, emerging technologies, and the human spirit.

name: Kristen Gaylord
title: Herzfeld Curator of Photography and Media Arts at the Milwaukee Art Museum
bio: Kristen Gaylord is the Herzfeld Curator of Photography and Media Arts at the Milwaukee Art Museum (MAM), where she recently organized Widline Cadet’s first solo exhibition at an American museum (2026) and Erin Shirreff: Permanent Drafts (2025), and serves as site curator for the Victoria and Albert Museum’s Arresting Beauty: Julia Margaret Cameron (2024). This year she opened Beneath the Surface: Mining and American Photography, a major survey of the relationship between photography and extractive industries in the United States from the 1840s until today, co-curated for the National Gallery of Art and currently on tour. Previously, Gaylord was a photography curator at the Amon Carter Museum of American Art, where she worked with artists including Stephanie Syjuco and Camille Utterback and brought landmark surveys of An-My Lê and Christina Fernandez to Fort Worth. Additionally, she co-organized Moving Pictures: Karl Struss and the Rise of Hollywood (2024), whose catalogue won the Deutscher Fotobuchpreis. Gaylord also held multiple curatorial roles at The Museum of Modern Art, New York, NY, where she contributed to exhibitions and publications including Stephen Shore (2017); Arbus Friedlander Winogrand: New Documents, 1967 (2017); and Ocean of Images: New Photography 2015. She holds an M.A. and a Ph.D. in art history from the Institute of Fine Arts at New York University. (Photo Credit: Ciara Elle Bryant)

name: Kristin Sieve
title: President
bio: Kristy Sieve is President + Partner and Graphic Design Lead at Mertz Design Studio, a Cincinnati-based brand strategy and design agency. A servant leader passionate about design, culture, and community, she helps guide the studio's creative vision and client partnerships.

name: Laurkita Sheffield
title: CFO and Small Business Empowerment Educator
bio: Laurkita Sheffield is an accountant, CFO strategist, financial empowerment educator, and founder of Sheffield Accounting & Financial Services. She helps small-business owners understand their numbers, improve cash flow, strengthen profitability, and make informed decisions about pricing, taxes, hiring, and growth. Through CFO-level advisory services, financial education programs, workshops, and strategy intensives, Laurkita transforms complex financial concepts into practical strategies entrepreneurs can confidently apply within their businesses. Laurkita is also the creator of the C.A.S.H.F.L.O.W. Framework™, a financial leadership system built around Clarity, Accountability, Strategy, Habits, Foundations, Leadership, Ownership, and Wealth, and the author of *The C.A.S.H.F.L.O.W. Framework™: Take Control of Your Cashflow*. Her work is rooted in helping entrepreneurs move beyond financial survival and develop the clarity, confidence, and control necessary to build businesses that are profitable, financially stable, and prepared to last.

name: Lawrence Malott - FOREALISM
bio: Forealism is a father-and-son creative duo consisting of Lawrence and Thomas Malott, working across DJing, costume design, performance art, music, and visual installations. Their multidisciplinary practice blends sound, movement, and handmade, often recycled materials to create immersive, otherworldly experiences centered on audience engagement and personal expression. A defining element of their work is the integration of light through reflective, illuminated costumes and their signature DJ installation, the “Light Ship,” which extends their performative process into a shared space with audiences. Since forming in 2012, they have performed internationally at venues and festivals including the Cincinnati Art Museum, Riverfest, Art Basel Miami, and LIV Miami, while continually evolving their practice between music production and live performance.

name: Lekha Challappa
title: Founder/CTO
bio: Lekha Challappa is the Founder of Aurat, a venture-backed company using AI to understand and predict how the brain responds to sensory inputs. Aurat is starting with scent, working with leading CPG and fragrance companies to transform how products are tested with consumers. Lekha’s vision is to build a broader platform for simulating human perception across the senses. She holds a graduate degree in AI from Emory University, focusing on computational neuroscience.

name: LeMonde Studio
bio: LeMonde Studio is a multidisciplinary creative practice that designs and produces large-scale, light-based installations that bring people together through play, energy, and collective wonder. Our work exists at the intersection of art, design, and technology, transforming light into a medium for connection and storytelling. Based on collaboration and innovation, we partner with local musicians, visual artists, and engineers to create experiences that respond to human interaction and the rhythm of community life.

name: Leonard Harmon
bio:
Leonard Harmon has always been drawn to a life of expression. Leonard credits a large part of his passion too. As he puts it, his “direct bloodline to art”. His father was a furniture maker, and his uncle, and namesake Leonard Allen Harmon, was a well-known portrait artist featured in the Heard Museum of Arizona. Art, in one form or the other, was always present in his life. As a young man, he was inspired by his grandparents' love of cooking to attend Johnson & Wales University, one of the finest culinary schools in the country, where he not only learned the fine art of creating culinary masterpieces but also began to explore his love of music. Eventually touring the country as a DJ, it wasn’t until 2010 that Leonard began to explore a new form of expression, traditional and contemporary mixed media.

In an interview with The Stranger, Leonard explains, “I like using older images to tell a new story of putting perspective on our history. As a new artist, I like exploring all kinds of methods and mediums. Each new style I incorporate helps me express myself in a new way. I’m never scared to try new things and see where my mind takes me.”

A citizen of the Lenape Tribe of New Jersey and the Nanticoke Tribe of Delaware, Leonard currently lives on the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indian Reservation. He reflects often on traveling to Connecticut and Oklahoma to attend Powwows and be immersed in his culture. He continues to be actively involved in tribal traditions on the Siletz Reservation. This immersion is seen in his work as he takes inspiration from his ancestors to put modern spins on traditional arts.
notes: Also "Leonard D. Harmon (Nanticoke)", curator of the Indigenous Peoples’ Day Convergence exhibition; the CAC calendar calls him "Leonard “Lenny” Harmon, CAC's Fall Co-LAB artist".

name: Leslie Epsztein
bio: Leslie Epsztein is a French designer from Bordeaux who specializes in projection mapping. After studying art, performing arts, and visual communication in France, she spent five years working with video artist Xavier de Richemont before launching her independent practice in 2015. Since then, she has created and contributed to large-scale light installations for cities and festivals across Europe and the United States, blending themes of time, space, science, dreams, and mythology with local cultural narratives. Drawing on her background in illustration, cinema, and graphic design, her work combines painterly and graphic visual styles with a strong emphasis on storytelling and musical rhythm.

name: Leslie Mooney
title: Vice President and Executive Director, BLINK
bio: Mooney has served as Executive Director of the Clifton Cultural Arts Center since 2013, and among other accomplishments, spearheaded the building of its new home in the heart of Clifton. She was also Development Director at the National Underground Railroad Freedom Center and, while living in Washington, DC and Boston, held positions at the US Department of Justice and Boston History & Innovation Collaborative. Her career has focused on building civic connection through storytelling, placemaking, and inclusive arts and cultural programming.

name: Lia Lubinsky
title: Assistant designer
org: University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music (CCM), Lighting Design and Technology
bio: Lia Lubinsky is a fourth-year Lighting Design and Technology Major at the University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music. During her years attending UC she has had the opportunity to work on many productions in a variety of roles. She has also had the opportunity to intern at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony in Los Angeles, California in 2025. Lia is grateful to be able to study and pursue her passion, and to learn along-side talented and promising young professionals. After graduating, she hopes to go into concert and festival lighting design and programming. She is very excited for the opportunity to work alongside Jacob Kaplan, Lucy Dunn and Jack Walter for BLINK 2026, and hopes that you stop by and take a look.
notes: Member of the CCM student team behind "Echoes of Light" (UC News, 2026-08-08). BLINK has not published an individual page.

name: Lightborne
bio: Lightborne is a creative-led design, animation, & production studio specializing in visuals for tours & live events, commercial & branded content, and installation & immersive experiences. Our studio works as a fully integrated creative partner, uniting specialists in motion design, animation, live-action production, experiential media, graphic design, projection mapping, and large-scale technical execution. Our disciplines work together with intention, precision, and a creative vision that defines our work, ensuring each project invites audiences into an experience that feels purposeful, engaging, and enduring. It would be our honor to participate in BLINK once again. We put all of our hearts into it each year and it means the world to us, the city and the region.

name: Lindsay Albert
title: Program Manager, KADIST
bio: Lindsay Albert is a curator and arts producer based in San Francisco, CA, currently serving as Program Manager at KADIST. Her career spans the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, McEvoy Foundation for the Arts, and Minnesota Street Project. Albert has curated notable exhibitions including Makeshift Memorials, Small Revolutions presented at KADIST and the Blaffer Art Museum (Houston, TX), Natural Fictions at The Carnegie (Covington, KY), and produced solo presentations by Indira Allegra, Leila Weefer, and Ragnar Kjartansson. In 2023, Albert co-founded staircase, an alternative project space exclusively presenting female and non-binary artists in the Bay Area. Her curatorial practice is rooted in Romantic conceptualism and the poetics of memory, and the intersection of art and social discourse. (Photo Credit: Jenna Garrett)

name: Lindsay Glatz + William Nemitoff
bio: Lindsay Glatz is a visual storyteller dedicated to bringing wonder and vibrancy into public space, often drawing on themes of childhood and nostalgia to explore human connection. William Nemitoff, founder of Curious Form, combines expertise in materials, construction methods, science, and technology to develop innovative collaborative artworks and public installations. Together, their studio practice bridges art, architecture, and fabrication, transforming ambitious concepts into built realities through precise craftsmanship and digital fabrication. Their work—especially in light-based installation—merges advanced technology with hands-on making to create striking, durable environments that invite wonder, interaction, and connection.

name: Lindsay Karas Stencel
title: New Ventures Partner
bio: Lindsay is a partner in the New Ventures practice at Thompson Hine and chairs the Private Fund Formation group. She advises entrepreneurs, investors, and fund managers on a wide range of venture capital and startup matters, including fund formation, mergers and acquisitions, corporate finance, securities compliance, and governance. Before joining Thompson Hine, she was a partner and chief legal counsel at a Midwest-focused venture capital firm, concentrating on deal structuring, portfolio management, fundraising, and exit transactions. Lindsay also managed her own private practice, representing emerging and diverse fund managers, startups, and investors nationwide. Her leadership roles at a venture development organization in upstate New York included serving as COO, CIO, CLO, and Managing Partner, where she helped establish and run one of the most active and largest seed funds in the region. Lindsay’s extensive legal, operational, and investment experience enables her to effectively address client needs. She also teaches at The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law and is a national speaker on topics of socioeconomic impacts on venture capital.

name: Liv Cassinelli
notes: Named in the BLINK 2026 participating-artists release; no artist page or linked artwork on blinkcincinnati.com yet (checked 2026-09-24).

name: Looking Up Arts
bio: This collaborative practice creates sculptural light installations that transform public spaces into immersive environments for shared discovery, blending art, engineering, and community engagement. Nearly all components are fabricated in-house, combining digital fabrication with hands-on craft to produce works that feel both precise and deeply human. Each project begins with a site and evolves into a responsive environment shaped by movement, sound, and participation, using light as both material and metaphor. The team’s origins trace back to a formative public artwork that shifted their focus from gallery-based work to community-centered installations, leading to a long-term partnership between Sri and Josh that merges technical expertise, scientific principles, and sculptural design into experiential works that invite connection and wonder.

name: Lucy Dunn
title: Assistant designer
org: University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music (CCM), Lighting Design and Technology
bio: Lucy Dunn is a lighting design technician focusing on installation and experience lighting design. Lucy is currently in their final year at the University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music working towards a BFA in Lighting Design and Technology. Lucy is originally from Baltimore Maryland and intends to be east coast based following graduation. During their time at CCM, they have worked on productions as a Assistant Production Electrician, including The Lightning Thief, Midsummer Night's Dream and Production Electrician for The Opera Double Bill and the upcoming Fall Dance Works and Cabaret. This summer they are working as a Design Intern for Lunar Telephone Company, focusing on installation projects. Outside of lighting design, Lucy enjoys painting in watercolor and acrylic, hiking, as well as jewelry making and clothing upcycling.
notes: Member of the CCM student team behind "Echoes of Light" (UC News, 2026-08-08). BLINK has not published an individual page.

name: Lynn Whitney
title: Associate Professor Emeritus
bio:
Lynn Whitney is a large format black-and-white film photographer working in the documentary tradition. Her photographs illuminate timeless questions central to the human search for meaning and purpose, grounded by the landscape and animals. Through diverse, but universally connected subject matter including soldiers in the military, sisters in the convent, family members, farmers, and birders, Whitney’s work addresses the mysterious air we share in community with one another.

Whitney earned her B.A. in American Culture Studies from Boston University, her B.F.A. in Photography from the Massachusetts College of Art and Design, and her M.F.A. from Yale School of Art. Her monograph, Lake Erie (2023) was published by Kehrer Verlag, Heidelberg, Germany, and a monograph featuring her convent photographs, published by Dust Collective, will be available early 2027.

Whitney has received commissions from the Toledo Museum of Art and The George Gund Foundation in Cleveland, and an Individual Artist Grant from the Ohio Arts Council. Her work is in the collections of the Toledo Museum of Art, OH; The George Gund Foundation, Cleveland, OH; the Museum of Contemporary Photography at Columbia College Chicago Midwest Photographers Project, IL; the Cleveland Clinic, OH; Ohio Humanities; Southeast Center for Photographic Studies, Daytona Beach, FL; and Yale University, New Haven, CT.

Whitney is Associate Professor Emeritus of Photography at Bowling Green State University, where she served as Photography area head in the School of Art for over thirty years. She now lives in Northwest Ohio. (Photo Credit: Kevin Vereecke)

name: Marie AJRAS
bio: Maria AJRAS is an Argentine muralist and visual artist currently based in Brooklyn, New York and working internationally across Argentina, Mexico, Europe, and the United States on large-scale public art projects. Her practice is rooted in the belief that art can reveal what is not yet visible, treating murals as collective thresholds where memory, identity, and emotion emerge into form through color, scale, and gesture. With a background in psychology, she approaches each work through deep listening and community dialogue, translating local narratives into poetic visual compositions that balance realism and abstraction. Her murals—often depicting monumental female figures—function as acts of visibility and reparation, transforming architecture into emotionally resonant spaces that reflect both personal and collective experience.

name: Mark Fleming
title: President
bio: Mark is a chartered financial analyst (CFA) and financial risk manager (FRM) with 20+ years of experience in investment management and business advisory, specifically for ultra-high-net-worth clients. His expertise spans trading, sector analysis, portfolio management, and succession planning, and as a small business owner himself, he has started, bought, built, and exited businesses across a range of industries. Mark is the president of Owner Actions and a board advisor to every portfolio business. He is also a youth soccer coach, a father to 3 boys, and an avid Ohio State fan.

name: Mark Gagas
title: COO/Co-Founder
bio: With more than 22 years in technology and automation, Mark leads Sensory Robotics’ operational and commercial execution as COO and co-founder. A U.S. military ARMY veteran, he drives strategy, partnerships, and revenue growth for SR-1, the company’s 3D sensing safety solution built to support fenceless, human-robot collaboration in real production environments. Mark is known for bridging engineering, certification, and customer needs, bringing disciplined execution to complex deployments and turning safety requirements into scalable solutions that protect people and keep lines running.

name: Mark Voytek
title: CEO Voytechnology Partners & Founding Partner Next Stage Trajectory
bio: Mark Voytek is Founder and Managing Partner of Voytechnology Partners and a strategic advisor to enterprises and high-growth technology companies based on his Founding Partner role with Next Stage Trajectory. A former EY Partner, Mark has spent more than 25 years leading and advising on business transformation, global business services, technology, and go-to-market growth. He is also an active startup advisor, investor, author, and guest lecturer who is passionate about mentoring the next generation of founders and business leaders.

name: Mary Mason Boaz
title: CEO & Founder
org: Mary Mason Boaz Coaching and Consulting
bio: Mary Mason Boaz is an executive coach and talent strategist who helps leaders build organizations where both people and performance thrive. With nearly two decades of experience spanning education, nonprofits, and high-growth organizations, she has led talent strategy, executive team development, and organizational growth through periods of rapid change. As a former Chief People and Program Officer and current executive coach, Mary Mason works with founders and senior leaders to navigate the leadership challenges that emerge as organizations grow and scale. Her approach combines organizational strategy with human behavior, helping leaders recognize the patterns that drive sustainable growth, not just short-term success. Mary Mason lives in Lexington with her husband and two young children. She is originally from Richmond, VA but has also called Washington, DC, Brooklyn, NY, and Charlotte, NC home. She is passionate about social justice and loves all things Bravo.

name: Mary Tighe
title: Founder and Marketing Strategist
bio: As a kid, Mary Tighe skipped the princess and dragon stories and went straight to interviewing her great-grandmother instead. That curiosity led her to journalism and, eventually, fifteen years in marketing. Today, Mary helps businesses make sense of what they do, find the stories beneath the surface and turn it all into marketing that sounds like them.

name: Mason Clutter
title: Partner
bio:
Mason Clutter is a Partner and Privacy Lead at FBT Gibbons. Her work focuses on the intersection of data security, privacy, and technology. A pivotal member of the firm’s AI and AI Governance team, Mason offers nearly years’ experience as a lawyer and policy advocate in Washington, DC. She delivers actionable advice on privacy and data security, including legal compliance, policy and program development, and complex issues where privacy, security, and technology converge. Mason is a Certified Information Privacy Professional (CIPP/US, CIPP/E) with unique insight into policymaking, providing practical guidance that aligns with client objectives and is easily implemented.

Previously, Mason served as Chief Privacy Officer at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, advising senior leaders and the National Security Council on privacy implications for national security and law enforcement. She shaped and executed policies around emerging technologies and personal data, including AI, commercial data, and privacy-enhancing technologies, balancing innovation with federal privacy compliance. She managed data breach responses, cybersecurity incidents, and oversaw DHS’s FOIA program and training.

Mason also held key roles at the U.S. Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board, serving as Attorney-Advisor, Counselor to Board Member Ed Felten, and Acting Executive Director, and was detailed to the Office of the Director of National Intelligence for FOIA and civil litigation. Her prior experience includes serving as National Security and Privacy Counsel for the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, Rule of Law Counsel at the Constitution Project, and research at Yale Law School’s Lowenstein International Human Rights Clinic.

Mason’s deep expertise in privacy law and her experience advising government leaders empower her to deliver innovative strategies that help clients meet regulatory demands and mitigate privacy risks.

name: Matine Yuksel
title: Co-Founder & COO
bio: Matine Yuksel is the co-founder & COO of Beltways, an American OEM that designs, builds, operates, and maintains the world's only accelerators.

name: Matt Brady
title: Managing Director
bio: Senior at Miami University- Managing Director at Redhawk Ventures

name: Matthew Robben
title: CTO & Co-Founder
bio: Matthew Robben is the Co‑founder and CTO of Serif  Health, where he leads the development of pipelines and platforms that transform complex healthcare price‑transparency machine‑readable files into user-friendly, actionable insights. He is passionate about driving practical improvements in how payers, providers, and employers leverage price transparency.

name: Max Dworin
title: Vice President
bio: Max Dworin serves as a Vice President at Cintrifuse Capital, a $180mm AUM fund, where he leads investment into seed-stage companies in the Cincinnati region. Immediately prior to joining Cintrifuse, Max served as an Entrepreneur-in-Residence at Northern Kentucky-based startup hub Blue North. Max is a seasoned startup operator, having co-founded and served as COO of Onda, a tequila seltzer brand that scaled to national distribution and raised over $20 million in venture capital funding. Prior to working in startups, Max served as Press Secretary to U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer. Max received a BA from The Johns Hopkins University and an MBA from Yale School of Management. He is a recipient of the Cincinnati Business Courier’s 40 Under 40 Award and is a member of the 50th cohort of the Cincinnati Regional Chamber’s Leadership Cincinnati program.

name: Max Sansing
bio: Max Sansing is a Chicago-based fine artist and one of the city’s most prolific and talented muralists. His distinct aesthetic fuses the color-drenched dynamism of street art with the technical elegance of photorealism. Born and raised on the South Side by two artistic parents, Sansing discovered his passion and creative gift at an early age. During his youth he was involved with several graffiti crews and taught himself oil painting before completing formal training at the American Academy of Art. In addition to his studio practice, Sansing is frequently commissioned to create large-scale murals and experiential installations across the country. He is deeply committed to supporting his Chicago community and is involved with numerous youth programs that expand arts opportunities in underserved areas. His work has been featured in gallery shows and special events in Chicago, New York, and Miami among others.

name: MEDIANERAS
bio: Medianeras is an artistic duo formed by architect Vanesa Galdeano (Argentina–Spain) and visual artist Analí Chanquía (Argentina), who have collaborated for more than fourteen years on large-scale public art projects. Their practice is rooted in the concept of “medianeras,” or side walls, which they reinterpret as spaces that connect rather than divide, using murals to foster connection, belonging, and collective identity within urban environments. Through color, geometry, and architectural sensitivity, they transform city walls into reflective surfaces that engage in dialogue with their social and spatial context. Working internationally across more than 20 countries, their large-format murals merge precision and human scale, turning public space into a site for visual rhythm, interaction, and shared experience.

name: Megan Dollenmeyer
title: Managing Associate Attorney
bio: Megan Dollenmeyer is a Managing Associate at FBT Gibbons LLP who advises startups, founders, and investors on federal tax matters, including QSBS, equity compensation, pass-through and corporate taxation, business restructurings, and M&A transactions. She serves as Vice-Chair of the S Corporation Committee of the American Bar Association Tax Section and as Co-Chair of the Cincinnati Bar Association Taxation Section. Megan regularly works with emerging growth companies and provides practical tax planning guidance to businesses and founders from formation through exit.

name: Megyn Norbut
title: Co-Founder & Producing Director (Cincinnati Art Week); Founder, No Standing
bio: Megyn Norbut was born to collaborate. For over a decade she has organized people, ideas, and all the moving parts needed to create intentional and meaningful events. Since founding No Standing, Megyn has built a strong reputation for producing progressive events that embody each client’s mission.

name: Melissa Smith
title: CEO
bio: Dr. Melissa Smith is an Associate Professor of Biochemistry and Molecular Genetics at the University of Louisville. After earning her PhD in Virology at Harvard and completing immunology training at the Institut Pasteur, she helped develop long-read single-molecule sequencing methods at Pacific Biosciences. She later served as Associate Director of Technology Development at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. Her start-up, Clareo Biosciences, founded in Louisville, Kentucky, in 2024, leverages proprietary genomics approaches and AI modeling to profile immune variation and predict therapy responsiveness and autoimmune risk from these "immune fingerprints" to support patient stratification in clinical trials, discovery of novel immune biomarkers, and implementation of precision medicine approaches.

name: Miami University
bio: At Miami University in Oxford, Ohio, the Immersive & Reactive Media Lab (MUXR) brings together students of design, animation, and creative technology to produce professional-scale media experiences. Operating within the Emerging Technology in Business & Design (ETBD) program, the lab functions as both classroom and production studio, where students gain hands-on experience in projection mapping, motion design, lighting integration, and real-time media systems. Each year, advanced students in the IMS 440 course sequence collaborate with entertainment industry partners, working in professional pipelines alongside studios such as Silent Partners Studio, XR Studios, Cour Design, and 4Wall Entertainment, and building pathways toward careers at leading companies in the field.

name: Michael Carrico
title: LEARNING & DEVELOPMENT
bio: Michael Carrico is the Engineering & AI Learning & Development Director at 84.51˚, a retail data science, insights, and media company. In this role, he leads initiatives to enhance the skills and capabilities of technical professionals within the organization. Under his leadership, 84.51˚ has achieved significant advancements in learning engagement and skill development, as evidenced by their recognition in the Degreed Visionary Awards in 2025. Prior to his current position, Michael served as a Data Science Director, Senior Analyst, and Senior Developer at 84.51˚, demonstrating his proficiency in data analysis and software development. He holds a Master of Science in Business Informatics from Northern Kentucky University and a Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the University of Kentucky.

name: Michelle Murcia
title: Founder + CEO
bio:
Michelle has more than 25 years of finance, accounting, administration and investment experience, in publicly traded, privately held and not for profit corporations, startups and billion-dollar enterprises, regional investment funds, investment advisory service firms and highly performing national funds. Michelle has served as a C-level consultant to early-stage start-up companies since 2013 providing strategic financial services as their contract Chief Financial Officer, advising on a number of complex financial transactions, and to an investment advisory firm as Venture Partner, supporting the investment process for Series B, C and later stage syndicated venture transactions, including due diligence, financial modeling, investment document preparation and portfolio reporting.

She launched Book+Street in early 2018 to address a big gap in the startup ecosystem in the Midwest, providing on-demand CFO and controllership services to a growing number of tech and service companies throughout Ohio.

Michelle is a Certified Public Accountant in addition to her Certified Equity Professional designation, earned a BS in Business Administration with an emphasis in Service Sector Management from California State University, San Marcos, and an MBA from The Ohio State University.

name: Mike Stasny
bio: Mike Stasny creates large-scale sculptures, inflatables, and installations that channel joy, absurdity, and a sense of childlike wonder. His work invites audiences into playful, immersive experiences that prioritize feeling and curiosity over fixed meaning, encouraging people to reconnect with creativity and awe. Rooted in the belief that fun can be a radical act, Stasny’s practice uses silliness and spectacle as tools for connection in a culture often driven by productivity over presence.

name: Mike Venerable
title: Director of Healthcare & Life Sciences
bio: Mike Venerable is Director of Healthcare & Life Sciences and a founding partner of The O.H.I.O. Fund, where he focuses on identifying and investing in companies with the potential to scale, create jobs, and drive long-term economic growth across Ohio. Mike brings more than two decades of experience as an entrepreneur, investor, company builder, and advisor. Prior to joining The O.H.I.O. Fund, he spent roughly 17 years with CincyTech, ultimately serving as President & CEO. During his tenure, he helped build and invest in emerging technology and life sciences companies and worked closely with entrepreneurs, research institutions, investors, and regional partners to strengthen Southwest Ohio's innovation economy. Before entering venture investing, Mike built his career as a software entrepreneur and investor. His professional journey has taken him from Ohio to California, South Korea, and the Washington, D.C. region, giving him a firsthand perspective on how technology, capital, talent, public policy, and strong networks can transform regional economies. An Ohio native, Mike returned to the state in 2004 and has spent much of the past two decades helping build its entrepreneurial ecosystem. Today, he leads The O.H.I.O. Fund's healthcare and life sciences efforts, connecting promising companies with the capital, expertise, and relationships needed to grow. A native of Hamilton, Ohio, Mike's passion for economic development is also personal. He has watched his hometown evolve from the decline of its traditional manufacturing base into a community experiencing renewed investment and growth, an experience that informs his belief that innovation and entrepreneurship can create opportunity throughout Ohio.

name: Mike Zelkind
title: Founder
org: CEO | Chairman | Board Member | VC & PE Advisor
bio:
Mike Zelkind is an entrepreneur and longtime food industry executive who co-founded Cincinnati-based 80 Acres Farms in 2015. Prior to launching 80 Acres, Mike spent more than 25 years in the food industry, holding leadership roles with companies including General Mills, Del Monte, Bumble Bee Foods and ConAgra.

At 80 Acres, Mike helped pioneer new approaches to indoor agriculture, combining technology, automation and food production to rethink how fresh food could be grown closer to consumers. Over the course of a decade, the company grew from an early Cincinnati startup into a nationally recognized name in vertical farming.

Mike remains a recognized voice at the intersection of food, technology, entrepreneurship and innovation, with deep roots in Cincinnati’s business and startup community.

name: Mindscape Studio
bio: Mindscape Studio is an award-winning multidisciplinary creative studio specializing in projection mapping, immersive experiences, event design, and interactive installations. Blending art, technology, and storytelling, the studio transforms architectural spaces into dynamic, multisensory environments that engage audiences through light, motion, and sound. From concept development to final execution, Mindscape Studio has created works for leading international festivals and cultural events, including Fête des Lumières, iMapp Bucharest, Festival of Lights Berlin, LUMA Projection Arts Festival, and the George Enescu Festival.

name: Mitko Karshovski
title: Director of Community Engagement / Founder
bio: Mitko Karshovski is the Director of Community Engagement at Blue North and SparkHaus where he helps support founders and the broader startup ecosystem. He's also the cofounder of Cincy Scoop, a local media company and venture studio.

name: Mz. Icar
bio:
Mz. Icar, an anonymous art collective predominantly comprised of Black Women, stands at the intersection of artistic innovation and societal transformation. Our collective name, “racIzM,” spelled backward, serves as a guiding principle, symbolizing our mission to upend conventional constructs of gender and race. We recognize these identifiers as fluid concepts, deeply influenced by the nuances of time, place, and context. They are not restrictions, but rather, perspectives through which we interpret the world, explore our identities, and drive our creative journey.

Our collective is an ensemble of multi-talented artists, each specializing in distinct roles within our creative process. Among us, skilled Illustrators, Photographers, Designers, Prop Stylists, Street Artists, and Collage Artists unite with a common vision. Together, we create art that celebrates the essence of Women, the global tapestry of Blackness, and the spirit of play.

Our artistic odyssey with Mz. Icar is a kaleidoscope of projects and creations. We’ve ventured into exhibitions, murals, public installations, augmented reality-activated public art, and brand collaborations, all bearing the indelible marks of play, color, composition, and a celebration of diverse narratives. Our murals span from local treasures to international marvels, infusing vibrancy and life into public spaces. Beyond this, we’ve directed an award-winning short film, “Of Expansion,” and lent our conceptual art and art direction to Ms. Lauryn Hill’s World Tour. Collaborations with renowned brands such as Doritos, BET, and Xbox have allowed us to infuse our artistic vision into various media.

name: Napoleon Maddox
bio: The artist’s interdisciplinary practice brings together multiple forms of production to explore subconscious dimensions of intimate relationships, colonial legacies, and acts of liberation. Visual art and object-making have been central to their life since childhood, shaped by parents who used creativity as both a problem-solving tool and a means of sustaining family life, even while questioning its viability as a profession. This tension informs the work as both an act of resistance—asserting presence and voice as a person of African descent—and as a continuation of inherited, resourceful making strategies. Working across painting and mixed media, the artist feels a particularly strong connection to repurposed and recycled papers, layering new narratives over materials already marked by prior stories, while drawing deeply from childhood memories and a lifelong relationship to nature and Southern agricultural heritage.

name: Nathaniel M. Stein
title: Curator of Photography at the Cincinnati Art Museum
bio: Nathaniel M. Stein, Ph.D., is Curator of Photography at the Cincinnati Art Museum (CAM). Stein earned degrees in art history from Wesleyan University and Brown University, where his doctoral research focused on the history of photography in India. He has organized exhibitions of historical and contemporary photography—including presentations in Cincinnati of the works of David Hartt and John Edmonds, Sohrab Hura, Gillian Wearing, the Kamoinge Workshop, and Hank Willis Thomas—and led the formation of the CAM’s Nancy Rexroth Collection. Recent publications include The Natural World (2022), The Levee: A Photographer in the American South (2020), and Interference: Andre Bradley and Paul Anthony Smith (2017), as well as contributions to Beyond Bollywood: 2000 Years of Dance in the Arts of South Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Himalayan Region (2022). Prior to arriving in Cincinnati, Stein held curatorial positions at the Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Rhode Island School of Design Museum. Locally, he serves on the ArtsWave Pride Steering Committee. (Photo Credit: Tim Tiebout)

name: Nicholas Archer
title: Vice President
bio:
Nicholas Archer – BIO Nicholas Archer has spent more than two decades across healthcare's full continuum, spanning operations, innovation, and commercialization. At Cincinnati Children's Hospital, he leads the translation of scientific discovery into real-world impact, moving innovations from bench to bedside through technology transfer and venture creation. His work sits at the intersection of operational excellence, financial sustainability, and patient need—a balance he's pursued whether restructuring care delivery networks, building digital platforms, or advising emerging companies.

A graduate of Oakwood University with an MBA from the University of Florida and executive education from Harvard Business School, Nick has served on numerous boards focused on healthcare access and community development. Outside of work, he's an avid cyclist and sports enthusiast who enjoys time with his family.

name: Nick Cramer
title: Founder and principal
bio:
Nick Cramer is the founder and principal of Cramer Office, a design studio where he works with early-stage founders ahead of inflection points to make the next version of their company feel inevitable. His work spans product, brand, engineering, and narrative. He's an EIR at Blue North, a former venture-backed founder at Harper, and was Head of Design at Ahalogy and a GM at Roadtrippers.

He's an EIR at Blue North, a former venture-backed founder at Harper, and was Head of Design at Ahalogy and a GM at Roadtrippers.

name: Norlynn Story
title: Assistant Vice President- Business Access Advisor
bio:
Norlynn Story is an Assistant Vice President and Business Access Advisor with U.S. Bank, bringing more than 20 years of banking experience to her work with entrepreneurs and small business owners across Ohio. Serving Cleveland, Columbus, and Cincinnati, she helps business owners navigate financial systems, access capital, strengthen financial readiness, and build sustainable banking relationships.

A passionate advocate for economic opportunity, Norlynn regularly leads financial education workshops and collaborates with community and economic development organizations to connect entrepreneurs with the resources, relationships, and tools needed to grow their businesses. She is known for her relationship-driven approach and commitment to helping individuals and communities thrive.

bio: Oliver Barrett is a Clio Award-winning artist and designer known for bold illustration, key art and portraiture. His clients include Nike, Netflix, Marvel Studios, A24, Apple, Disney, ESPN, Lucasfilm and Warner Bros.

name: Onda Studio
bio: Onda Studio is a new media art collective based in Italy working at the intersection of art, architecture, and technology. Led by Marcello Arosio—an architect, multimedia artist, and artistic director of Kernel Festival and AreaOdeon—the studio brings together visual designers, musicians, developers, and architects to explore how light, sound, and movement can shape shared human experiences. Their practice examines the relationship between people and digital art across physical and virtual dimensions, bridging the individual and collective through immersive installations and interactive environments. Through video mapping, light, lasers, sound, and mobile interfaces, Onda Studio transforms public space into participatory, living canvases that invite audiences to engage with and reflect on the interconnected systems that shape contemporary life.

name: Osamu James Nakagawa
title: Ruth N. Halls Distinguished Professor at Indiana University
bio: Osamu James Nakagawa was born in New York City, raised in Tokyo, and returned to the United States at age fifteen, when he moved to Houston, TX. His artistic practice moves fluidly between the personal and political, shaped by his transnational experience in both Japan and the United States. Nakagawa received his M.F.A. from the University of Houston in 1993 and is currently the Ruth N. Halls Distinguished Professor of Art at Indiana University Bloomington. Nakagawa is the recipient of numerous honors, including the 2009 Guggenheim Fellowship. His work has been exhibited nationally and internationally and is held in major public collections such as the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, NY; the George Eastman Museum, Rochester, NY; the Tokyo Photographic Art Museum; the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, TX; the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art; and others. He is represented by PGI, Tokyo. (Photo Credit: Elaine Miller)

name: Paper Acorn
bio: Jessica Wolf creates ceiling-suspended kinetic sculptures inspired by the vastness and patterns of the natural world, crafting immersive environments that evoke wonder, peace, and a sense of uplift. Using lightweight materials such as polycarbonate and synthetic paper, her sculptures balance strength and grace through movement and translucency, allowing light to cast ethereal shadows that transform her organic forms into dynamic, meditative experiences.

name: Parker Heyl
bio: Parker is an installation artist, kinetic sculptor, educator, and mechanical engineer whose work explores the relationship between physical objects and digital technologies in art, music, and architecture. Through kinetic sculptures and immersive environments, he examines what is lost when experiences are translated into digital form, emphasizing the presence and aura of physical objects. Trained as a carpenter and currently teaching at the Bartlett School of Architecture at University College London, he combines technical expertise with artistic inquiry to create thought-provoking electromechanical works. His installations and set designs have been presented internationally at leading galleries, festivals, and cultural events, including the Venice Biennale of Architecture, Munich Biennale, Salon del Mobile Milan, and Coachella Music Festival.

name: Pastel
bio: Francisco Diaz Scotto is a painter and architect (UBA) whose practice approaches public space through the concept of “urban acupuncture,” activating overlooked or neglected sites within the city. Working primarily in facades and other “non-places,” he transforms these surfaces into canvases that engage in dialogue with their surrounding environment. His work draws inspiration from resilient urban flora—plants that grow in sidewalk and wall cracks—using them as symbols to question rigid, exclusionary systems of urban design. By enlarging and recontextualizing these overlooked natural forms, he challenges modern notions of control in architecture while emphasizing a respectful, site-responsive relationship between artwork and environment.

name: Patrick Brown
title: Director of Commercialization
bio: Patrick J. Brown is Director of Commercialization at the University of Cincinnati's 1819 Innovation Hub, where he leads efforts to develop and commercialize UC technologies, research, and innovation — connecting entrepreneurs, industry partners, and investors with UC's deep portfolio of intellectual property, capabilities, and resources. Having licensed UC technology and co-founded a startup himself, Patrick now helps others do the same. With nearly two decades at UC, he has built a career around bridging the gap between the lab and the market and finding the right partners to bring UC innovations to life.

name: Patrick Longo
title: President / CEO
bio: Longo has been engaged with Alloy Development for over 30 years and was named President and CEO in 2019 after being the Vice President & Director of the Alloy Growth Lab, an innovation focused business incubation program. As the Growth Lab Director, Longo aided in the creation, development, and growth of over 300 entrepreneurial entities.

name: Paul Ehlinger
title: Founder/CEO
bio: Paul is a biomedical engineer that somehow got trapped in the world of startups and venture capital. He currently runs Flamel - automating marketing for multi-location brands. In his free time - he reads, studies (read drinks) wine, and cooks meals with his wife Lina.

name: Paul Jackson
title: SVP Strategic Programs
bio: Paul Jackson is the Senior Vice President of Strategic Programs at Entrepreneurs' Center (EC) in Dayton, Ohio, where he leads EC's Commercialization Team and has directly supported over 100 startups in licensing university- and federally-owned IP. He also co-teaches the University of Dayton's entrepreneurship capstone course, guiding students through market assessment and new venture creation based on university-derived technology. Paul's experience spans nearly 20 years across technology commercialization, economic development, and applied research policy — including managing Ohio Third Frontier's technology commercialization and R&D grant portfolio. That work has put him in direct, ongoing contact with technology transfer offices across the State and beyond, giving him a broad, cross-institutional view of what it takes to move research out of the lab and into the market.

name: Paul Mpagi Sepuya
title: Artist and Professor
bio: Paul Mpagi Sepuya is a Los Angeles-based artist working in photography. He is known for his New York portrait series from the early 2000s, later moving into studio-based projects that question and complicate questions of authorship, the visualization of race and sexuality, and the structures of the photographic medium. Sepuya’s work has been acquired by the Getty Museum, Los Angeles, CA; Los Angeles County Museum of Art; San Francisco Museum of Modern Art; The Museum of Modern Art, New York, NY; the Whitney Museum of American Art, New York, NY; the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York, NY; Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam; Tate Modern, London, England; the Victoria and Albert Museum, United Kingdom; and others. Solo museum exhibitions include Fotomuseum Amsterdam, PHOXXI at Deichtorhallen Hamburg, Germany; and surveys at the Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis, MO, and Nottingham Contemporary, United Kingdom. Focus. Desire., a survey of work from 2005–2025 was presented in 2026 at Fotomuseum Winterthur, Switzerland, and the Sprengel Museum in Hannover, Germany. His work has been covered and published in Artforum, Aperture, The New Yorker, The New York Times, Los Angeles Times, Art Review, Frieze, and Art in America. Sepuya is a Professor in Visual Arts and M.F.A. Program Director at the University of California San Diego, where he has taught since 2019.

name: Pete Millspaugh
title: Software Engineer & Writer
bio: Pete Millspaugh is a programmer and writer. He is currently working on his first book, “dot com et al: The Secret Life of Internet Domains,” and working at Val Town.

bio: Venture Capital Investor with Refinery Ventures, based in Cincinnati, Ohio.

name: Phillip Maisel
title: Artist
bio: Phillip Maisel utilizes site-informed materials to create sculpture, collage, video, and photographic objects. His work often subverts expectations of photographic space, destabilizing the viewer’s visual literacy. He received his M.F.A. from the California College of the Arts in San Francisco and his B.S. in Psychology from McGill University in Montreal, Canada. Maisel has presented solo exhibitions at the Chiquita Room, Barcelona, Spain; Gregory Lind Gallery, San Francisco, CA; Nazarian / Curcio (formerly Shulamit Nazarian), Los Angeles, CA; and DOCUMENT, Chicago, IL. He has exhibited at The William Benton Museum of Art at the University of Connecticut; the University of New Mexico, Taos; and the deCordova Sculpture Park and Museum, Boston, MA. His book, Two Concrete Things, received the ArtsLibris-Fundació Banc Sabadell Award in 2021. His work is included in the KADIST collection, as well as the High Museum, Atlanta, GA.

name: Polina Soloveichik
bio: Polina Soloveichik is a Berlin-based artist and muralist born in Russia and raised in the United States. She studied illustration at Pratt Institute in Brooklyn, where she first began painting murals and discovered a passion for creating art in public spaces. For more than 20 years, murals have been at the core of her artistic practice, allowing her to transform spaces and engage directly with communities. Her work can be found on walls large and small throughout Europe and the United States. Through site-specific projects, she explores the unique relationship between art, place, and the public.

name: Rachel DesRochers
title: Founder, CEO
bio:
Rachel DesRochers is a strategic advisor, community architect, transformational leader, consultant, connector, and the visionary founder of Power to Pursue, the Incubator Kitchen Collective and The Gratitude Collective – and she's passionate about empowering women and supporting entrepreneurs to build sustainable, purpose-driven businesses!

As an international speaker and recognized thought leader, Rachel shares her insights on entrepreneurship, strategic leadership, community building, gratitude, and women's empowerment with audiences worldwide. Her collaborative leadership style is key to her role as advisor for the Queen City Game Changers, an executive leadership program for women, where she develops and facilitates programming that mentors and guides emerging entrepreneurs and corporate leaders.

She's also the author of The Mourning Light: Reflections on Love and Loss and Shift to Light: 90 Days to Grateful, and creator of Gratitude Grams – a 54-card deck designed as practical tools for personal and professional transformation.

When she's not consulting, speaking, or building community, Rachel is being a mom to three wildly wonderful children who keep her grounded, grateful, and endlessly inspired!

name: Radius Concepts
bio: Radius Concepts is a design and fabrication studio specializing in furniture, sculpture, and architectural components for commercial and residential spaces, while also creating immersive public installations that transform ordinary environments into surreal experiences of light, humor, and communal play. Using materials such as steel, foam, sound, and illumination, the studio reimagines everyday interactions as moments of wonder, curiosity, and connection.

name: Rahul Desai
title: COO
bio: Rahul Desai is an operations executive who has spent the past decade helping people accelerate their careers and build smarter, stronger companies. He’s consulted at Google and Uber, scaled Silicon Valley startups to 100M+ valuations, sold an operations training business, served as an operating partner for a private equity fund, and now raised a fund of his own to build / buy group travel companies.

Rob is a member of the Cincinnati Commercial Products Practice and the Market Sector Leader for Tech and Services Sector for the firm’s Cincinnati, Louisville and Evansville markets. He has over 14 years of experience providing assurance and consulting services to companies in technology and services, manufacturing and consumer and logistics spaces.

He is a member of the American Institute of CPAs, The Ohio Society of Certified Public Accountants, and Association for Corporate Growth.

Rob is active in the community, having previously served on the board of the Nashville Sports Council and is a recent graduate of Leadership Northern Kentucky.

He is a graduate of University of Dayton, Ohio, with an M.B.A. degree and a B.S.B.A. degree in accounting.

name: Robyn Moore
title: Photomedia-based Artist
bio:
Robyn Moore is a photomedia-based artist living and working in eastern Kentucky. Her work explores how alternative and experimental photographic processes can reveal the unseen worlds around us, while her research investigates deep time, biosemiotics, geology, paleontology, phenomenology, and the ways in which images can help us facilitate understanding of and solidarity with other forms of life.

Moore’s work has been exhibited widely, including at the Jubilee Fifth International Print Biennale, Yerevan, Armenia; the South Australian Museum, Adelaine, Australia; Gold Street Studios Gallery, Victoria, Australia; the Centre for Print Research, Bristol, England; Houston Center for Photography, Soho Photo Gallery, New York, NY; The Halide Project, Philadelphia, PA; The Image Flow Photography Center, San Anselmo, CA; and Manhattan Graphics Center, New York, NY. Recent honors include selection as the 2024 South Arts Southern Prize and State Fellowship recipient for Kentucky, the 2025 Uncommon Art Residency Award at the Teton Art Lab in Jackson, WY, and a Great Meadows Foundation Artist Professional Development Grant. Moore’s work won the professional series alternative processes category at the 23rd Julia Margaret Cameron Awards for Women Photographers.

Moore holds a Ph.D. in Visual Arts from the University of Sydney and an M.F.A. in Photography and Experimental Film from the School of the Museum of Fine Arts at Tufts University. She is currently an Associate Professor of Photography at Morehead State University in Morehead, KY.

name: Rolando Archila
title: Founder
bio: Rolando Archila teaches founders to make their ideas impossible to ignore. As the founder of SLIDEAS, he has helped founders and executives raise more than $1 billion through pitch decks and narratives built for high-stakes moments. His clients range from seed-stage startups to C-suites at Fortune 500s such as Nestlé, Clorox, Johnson & Johnson, and Kimberly-Clark. His thesis is simple: as AI makes content infinite, genuinely human stories become invaluable. That's why he now coaches founders and executive teams on human-first, AI-assisted workflows that sharpen thinking and structure narratives investors actually remember.

name: Ryan Vaughan
title: Partner
bio: Ryan has over 18 years of diversified public accounting experience providing tax and consulting experience to emerging, mid-market, and large multi-national companies. As a partner in the firms Federal Tax Specialty group, Ryan focuses on providing tax planning solutions to companies in a multitude of industries including manufacturing and distribution, energy, technology, real estate, retail, financial services, and health care. Ryan is a member of the American Institute of CPAs, and Tennessee Society of CPAs. Ryan is a graduate of Illinois Wesleyan University with a B.A. degree in accounting and DePaul University with a MBA and M.S. in Taxation.

name: Saad Ghosn
title: Founder and President at SOS Art

name: Sarah Dowlin
title: Founder &Creative Director
bio: Sarah Dowlin is a photographer by trade, an observer by nature, and the founder of WorkLife Studios. For nearly two decades, she’s worked inside organizations of all kinds, developing an eye for the moments, relationships, and patterns that reveal far more about a business than its marketing ever could. Today, her work explores one simple question: how can marketing help people feel known in a world obsessed with being seen? Through WorkLife Studios and her writing and speaking, Sarah explores Connection Marketing, relationship-led growth, storytelling, and the practice of paying attention.

name: Sarah Nazzal
title: Foresight Researcher
org: The Foresight Lab, University of Cincinnati
bio: Sarah Nazzal is a Chemical Engineering student at the University of Cincinnati pursuing an M.S. in Cosmetic Science through the ACCEND program. As a NEXT Innovation Scholar and Foresight Researcher, she is interested in the intersection of science, technology, healthcare, and emerging innovation. Her experience spans cancer research, environmental health, process engineering, and innovation-focused projects, and she enjoys exploring how new technologies can address real-world problems. She is particularly interested in learning from entrepreneurs and innovators and connecting with others building the future of healthcare, science, and technology.

name: Sarah Schmidt
bio: Sarah Schmidt is a Chicago-based cartoonist, animator and director known for playful, distinctive motion work. Co-founder of Sunshine Mall, creating projects for major clients, agencies and brands including Adult Swim and Bath & Body Works

name: Scott Edsall
title: Food Innovation Incubator Manager
bio: Scott Edsall has been with the Corporation for Findlay Market for three years, most recently as the Findlay Market Incubator Manager. During his tenure he has worked on the buildout of the Findlay Launch storefronts and incubated multiple businesses out of the Findlay Kitchen, most notably Soul Secrets and The Empanada’s Box. Scott also led the restoration of a 1970s deck oven, allowing new bakeries to start in the Kitchen. Scott has over 20 years of experience starting and operating food services in Cincinnati, Nashville and Illinois, with a focus on efficient operations for food businesses “Within one-on-one business mentoring, our goal is to lower the barrier of entry for businesses to start and thrive. We are trying to figure out programs, manuals–anything we can do that explains how to operate a food business, because that doesn’t exist.”

name: Scott Pennington
bio: Scott Pennington is a Baltimore-based artist specializing in large-scale participatory installation and sculptural assemblage works. Drawing upon his background as a furniture and cabinet-maker, Pennington utilizes woodworking and construction techniques to create colorful, detailed works of art that engage varied audiences and invigorate public spaces. Pennington’s work suggests a tangible, yet illusory reality that examines labor, consumer culture, the pursuit of simple pleasures, and the construction of nostalgic human connections both genuine and fictitious.

name: Sean Van Praag
bio: Sean began his career in 2008 after earning a degree in digital art and design and joining renowned film title artist and director Kyle Cooper at Prologue in Los Angeles. After honing his skills in film, commercial, and animation work, he launched his own studio, where he continues to work as a director, designer, and animator. His diverse client portfolio includes Nike, Greenies, Exxon Mobil, Left 4 Dead, and artists including Justin Bieber, Jay-Z, Katy Perry, Pitbull, and Fitz and The Tantrums. Since 2013, Sean has increasingly focused on projection art, creating commissioned work for festivals including Digital Graffiti and eight other projection art festivals across the country. His vibrant, playful artwork embraces experimentation and reflects the energy and stimulation of today’s digital world, with the goal of creating something novel that makes viewers smile.

name: Sew Valley
bio: Sew Valley is a Cincinnati-based nonprofit collective of designers, patternmakers, prototypers, samplemakers, and sewists who create immersive, large-scale textile installations using repurposed materials. Their work combines craftsmanship, sustainability, and storytelling, transforming everyday fabrics into dynamic environments that engage audiences through texture, color, movement, and light. By integrating illuminated textiles, projection surfaces, and interactive design elements, Sew Valley creates memorable experiences that foster curiosity, connection, and community engagement.

name: Shahryar Qureshi
title: Founder
bio: Shahryar (Shar) Qureshi is the founder and CEO of QURE, an Execution Intelligence Platform for Human-Critical Work. He holds a BS from Miami University, an MS from Wright State University, and spent 9+ years across academic, DoD and industry laboratories, followed by 5+ years in corporate development. He also serves as adjunct faculty at Wright State University's Boonshoft School of Medicine.

name: Shahzia Sikander
bio: Born in Lahore, Pakistan in 1969, Shahzia Sikander trained in traditional miniature painting during a period when the medium was largely out of favor with younger artists under the military regime of Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq. She earned her B.F.A. in 1991 from the National College of Arts (NCA) in Lahore, where she studied under master miniaturist Bashir Ahmad and later became the first woman to teach in the Miniature Painting Department. During her time at NCA, she emerged as a pioneering figure within the discipline, challenging its technical and aesthetic boundaries, with her early work The Scroll (1989–90) receiving major national recognition and awards that helped elevate the medium within contemporary art discourse. She later moved to the United States to pursue an M.F.A. at the Rhode Island School of Design, followed by participation in the CORE Program at the Glassell School of Art, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.

title: Faculty advisor; CCM Associate Professor of Lighting Design and Technology
org: University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music (CCM)
