name: Shelby Sinclair
title: Assistant Professor of African and African American Studies and History at the University of Virginia
bio: Shelby Sinclair is a historian of the 19th and 20th century United States and Caribbean. She specializes in histories of the U.S. empire, military occupation, gender, and visual culture in the Caribbean and its diasporas. Her current book project explores Haitian women’s lives and labors during the 19-year U.S. military occupation of Haiti (1915–1934). (Photo Credit: Raisa Chowdhury).

name: Sierra Hayden
title: Founder | CEO
bio: Sierra Hayden is the founder and CEO of We Outside, a Cincinnati outdoor lifestyle brand headquartered at The Basecamp in Over-the-Rhine. Her path runs through graphic design, fine art, and regenerative agriculture, an unusual mix that shapes how she builds brands, spaces, and community. She started the company on a simple observation, most people never picture themselves outdoors because nobody ever showed them how to start, and built We Outside to be that starting point. What began as community hikes has grown into a full lifestyle ecosystem, events, product, community, all built in Cincinnati for anyone who’s ever felt like they needed permission to be outside.

name: Silent Partners Studio
bio: As directors, designers, producers, and creatives, they specialize in visual storytelling, with two decades of experience creating imagery across every facet of the entertainment industry. Operating as a fully integrated design and production studio, they develop cutting-edge stagecraft for both in-person and virtual experiences, spanning music videos, world tours, television, theater, runway shows, sports and esports events, brand activations, corporate presentations, museums, and large-scale installations. Working from ideation through installation, they collaborate closely with clients to create bespoke turnkey and à la carte solutions that merge creative direction, production, set design, and content integration. Their practice is rooted in exploring the intersection of art and technology, using tools such as TouchDesigner, Notch, Unreal Engine, and generative AI to create immersive, interactive environments that invite audiences to actively engage within evolving spatial experiences.

name: Simion Collins
title: Film Director
bio:
I’m Simion Collins, a Cincinnati native and filmmaker with over 13 years of experience.

As the oldest of four siblings, I grew up navigating housing instability and early responsibility while helping support my sisters and brother. Those lived experiences shaped my understanding of resilience, empathy, and the importance of being seen.

Filmmaking became both a creative outlet and a way to reclaim control over my own narrative.

name: Smash Studio
bio: SMASH is a boutique, Stockholm-based experience design studio that creates large-scale projection mapping and interactive installations, blurring the boundaries between technology and architecture. Rooted in music, visual design, and motion graphics, the studio uses light, shadow, and sound to transform public spaces into shared, living experiences. Its collaborative team includes Ash Reed (Design Director), Veronica Reed (Account Director and Project Manager), Emile Pascoe (Lead Technical Artist), and Jonas Johansson (Lead Technical Director), who together shape the studio’s creative direction, technical development, and client relationships. Through real-time graphics, motion design, and custom interactive systems, SMASH develops emotionally resonant environments that invite audiences to engage, explore, and participate, turning architecture into dynamic canvases for collective experience.

name: Sofles
bio: Russell Fenn, better known as Sofles, is an Australian graffiti artist originating from Brisbane. Self-taught, he has been honing his skills for over 20 years, exploring various mediums such as spraypaint, acrylic, drawing and brush painting, as well as digital and illustration works.

name: Spencer Sterling
bio: Spencer Sterling is a multidisciplinary artist and machine learning researcher whose work transforms musical experiences into immersive visual environments. His practice explores the dialogue between music, space, and light, bridging real-time 3D graphics, artificial intelligence, and laser-based installations. Through his work with Silent Partners Studio, he has created visual content for performances by artists including Beyoncé, Celine Dion, and Muse, while his personal practice focuses on translating internal interpretations of music into spatial form. His process moves from 3D environments into custom-developed AI models and ultimately into dynamic laser installations that trace evolving digital compositions, reflecting an ongoing exploration of how sound can be experienced through light and space.

name: Stefan Chinov
title: Professor, School of Fine and Performing Arts

name: Stephanie Jenkins
title: Vice President, Strategic Planning and Operations
bio:
Responsibilities Stephanie is Vice President, Strategic Planning & Operations for Kroger Technology & Digital, based in Cincinnati, Ohio. Stephanie oversees strategic planning and portfolio management for Kroger’s Technology and Digital organization and is also responsible for the development, execution, and implementation of strategic partnership and M&A opportunities designed to accelerate Kroger’s strategic priorities in the Technology & Digital space.

Experience Stephanie joined The Kroger Co. in 2011 as a business operations leader at Kroger joint venture dunnhumbyUSA with responsibilities for business planning and implementation of key strategic and operational initiatives. Prior to her current role, she led the development and execution of key strategic partnerships for 84.51° to expand its commercial business and capabilities by utilizing assets and capabilities to create alternative profit streams through new and existing partnerships. Prior to joining Kroger, Stephanie was an engagement manager for KPMG LLP’s advisory services practice where she specialized in enterprise risk services for retail and technology clients.

Recognition Stephanie represents Kroger on the Cintrifuse Board of Directors and has participated in leadership development programs throughout the city including as a YWCA Rising Star. Education Stephanie holds a bachelor’s degree from Miami University. Personal Stephanie lives in Cincinnati with her husband and three children.

name: Stephanie von Ohain
title: Founder
bio: Stephanie is the founder of Ascension Analytics, where she helps growing businesses turn fragmented data into clear, confident decision-making. With nearly 20 years of experience in analytics leadership, she most recently led the Marketing Analytics team at Amazon Web Services (AWS) before founding Ascension Analytics. She specializes in translating complex data into practical business insights, helping founder-led businesses build simple measurement systems, align teams around meaningful metrics, and drive sustainable growth through clarity and action.

name: Strangeloop
bio: Strangeloop Studios is a visual content production company focused on working with creatives to explore new media and audience experiences. Their team is composed of animators, designers, producers, writers, musicians, and developers.

name: Sue Bevan Baggott
title: Founder & President
bio:
Sue Bevan Baggott is a human-centered Executive Advisor, Innovation Catalyst, and Intentional Investor. Sue is dedicated to empowering leaders to create positive impact, accelerate life-improving innovation, and invest in transformative change. Her career spans global innovation leadership at Procter & Gamble (growing mega-brands from Pantene and Pampers) to founding Power Within Consulting, a firm focused on human-centered strategies for meaningful leadership and business success.

As an “accidental angel investor” and startup advisor, Sue supports diverse portfolios of innovative startups addressing critical global challenges. She also advocates for inclusion in entrepreneurship and investing as an Associate Producer of Show Her the Money, a multi-award-winning documentary promoting investment in underrepresented founders. Through speaking, writing, consulting, advising, and board roles, Sue strives to inspire purposeful leadership and meaningful innovation. She also encourages more open discussions about money confidence and investing to encourage more people to build wealth through investing with their values to drive positive change.

Sue is a member of multiple early-stage investment groups and funds including: QCA Ventures, Next Wave Impact (Investment Committee member), Kachuwa Impact Fund, Mindshift Capital (LPAC member), Ohio Impact Fund (LP), H Venture Partners (LP), Fireroad Ventures (LP), SoGal Ventures (LP), Emmeline Ventures (LP), and Sage Growth Capital (LP). She’s also an Advisor for Accelerating Angels and several purpose-driven startups.

name: Susan Kosti
bio: Susan Kosti (Zsuzsanna Koszti), born on September 20, 1986 in Paris, is an award-winning international media artist and art director working globally. Her work explores the tension between humanity, science, technology, and spirituality, with the aim of reconnecting people to their environment through immersive experiences. She began her career in 2010 as a video designer for live events before expanding into music video direction and an internationally recognized short science fiction film. Over time, she has developed a distinctive visual language combining highly detailed forms, graphic design, and animation, with installations presented at major venues and festivals including Moment Factory projects, Tokyo Disneyland, UAE National Day 51, Vivid Sydney, and Blink Festival. In recent years, she has also been invited to collaborate with artists such as Es Devlin and has served as art director for major international pavilions and large-scale projection mapping works across global exhibitions.

name: Tab Benoit
title: Blues guitarist, Soul of the Swamp Tour

name: Take a Moment Studio
bio: Take a Moment Studio is an ongoing Cincinnati-based collaboration between artists Joe Walsh and Jon Flannery, combining hand-cut screen printing with hand-drawn illustration to create one-of-a-kind posters. Their work has included a residency at Cincinnati’s Contemporary Arts Center and public art collaborations throughout the region

name: Tammie Scott
title: Founder
bio: Tammie Scott is the founder and CEO of RiffPay, a fintech platform streamlining booking and payments for independent venues, event organizers, and artists — an idea born from her experience owning Nostalgia Wine & Jazz Lounge, an upscale wine bar and live music venue in downtown Cincinnati. She has spent 15 years in sports and entertainment marketing, including roles at the NFL Players Association and Roc Nation. Tammie is an alumna of Ohio University and Howard University.

name: Tassie Katherine Hirschfeld
title: Professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Oklahoma

name: The Great Paper Massacre
bio: The Great Paper Massacre is an artist whose practice is driven by an ongoing process of experimentation and creative exploration. A member of the Truly Design collective since 2018, their multidisciplinary work spans graphic design, illustration, painting, motion graphics, video, and experimental animation. Centered on collage as both a visual technique and conceptual framework, their practice draws inspiration from music, literature, and punk and Dadaist traditions. Working under the moniker The Great Paper Massacre, they use a deliberately provocative identity to deconstruct and reassemble visual language, investigating how images and ideas function by taking them apart.

name: The University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music – Lighting Design & Technology
bio: University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music (CCM) – Lighting Design and Technology prepares the next generation of lighting designers, programmers, technicians, and creative professionals through hands-on, experiential learning. Students gain real-world production experience across theater, dance, opera, film, concerts, and live events while working with industry-standard technology and faculty with extensive professional expertise. As one of the nation's premier performing arts institutions, CCM fosters innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence across the entertainment industry.

name: Theresa Bembnister
title: Independent Curator
bio: Theresa Bembnister is an independent curator and art writer based in Cleveland, OH. Previously, she served in curatorial roles at the Contemporary Arts Center in Cincinnati, the Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts in Little Rock, the Akron Art Museum, and the Beach Museum of Art in Manhattan, KS. (Photo Credit: Jason Masters)

name: Theresa Leininger-Miller
title: Professor of Art History at the University of Cincinnati

name: This is Loop
bio: Loop is the collaborative artistic partnership of artists Harriet Lumby and Alan Hayes. Based in their Somerset studio they have established a reputation for creating large scale experiential installations. With over thirty years combined practice focussing on utilising reflections and illusion at the intersection of technology, science and art this has created a common theme throughout their visually impactful architectural style work. Their installations invite audiences to be engulfed by intense and thought provoking choreographed audio visual journeys. Frequently working collaboratively with sound artists and musicians has helped to elevate their work allowing deeper exploration of ideas and concepts and enhancing the bond between audience members and the works themselves. They have a track record in creating both large scale site specific work as well as touring installations and have successfully done this in both the UK and internationally.

name: Tian Philson
title: Founder, Leadership Transformation Coach
bio:
Tian Philson is a Jay Shetty Certified Leadership Transformation and Decision-Making Coach and creator of the VOICCE® Framework - a proprietary method that helps leaders navigate uncertainty with clarity and confidence. With 20 years of corporate experience across CPG, Retail, and Media and as the founder of Love, Strength & Fitness, LLC, she blends mindfulness and strategy to help professionals lead authentically, confidently and sustainably. Tian is also a registered yoga teacher and passionate advocate for purposeful, holistic growth.

“We help leaders go inward, so they can go Upward.”

name: Tiffany Cooper
title: Community Impact Advisor (Creative Collaborator)
bio: Tiffany is a seasoned community connector with over two decades of experience fostering meaningful engagement across diverse groups. Her work spans curating impactful events, facilitating workshops and trainings, and collaborating with a wide range of stakeholders—including artists, students, and business leaders.
notes: Shares the Community Impact Advisor credit with Candra Reeves (Meaningful Connections). Headshot = uncaptioned portrait (1455x2000) on her own site's About page, placed directly above her signed quote ("— Tiffany"); no photographer credit. Her site links only the Meaningful Connections accounts (Instagram @meaningfulconnects, a Facebook page), not personal profiles.

name: Tim Hori
title: CEO
bio: Tim’s background in business has been entrepreneurial throughout his career. Even within established companies, he has consistently identified opportunities and developed new areas of business. He has worked across a wide range of industries, including radio, telecommunications, hospitality, restaurants, and healthcare. The diversity of these experiences has enabled Tim to quickly learn and adapt to unfamiliar industries while recognizing that the fundamentals of building a successful business are remarkably consistent. He understands what it takes to take a business from concept to launch and from startup to successful day-to-day operations.

name: Tim Metzner
title: Founding Partner
bio:
Tim Metzner is a serial entrepreneur (x5), father (x4), husband (x1), and follower of Jesus. He believes business can and should be a force for good in the world.

Tim is the founder of Fireroad, a pre-seed fund focused on founders who are helping SMBs stay local, scale efficiently, and compete in the AI economy.

Previously, Tim co-founded Coterie Insurance, a fast-growing small-business insurance company that has raised more than $200 million in capital and is growing profitably. He also co-founded Differential, an early venture studio that helped launch several successful companies, including Astronomer, now valued at more than $1 billion, and Apollos, a digital platform for churches.

Tim also founded OCEAN Accelerator which helped launch 80 companies over a decade supporting both founders and their companies.

A graduate of the Lindner Business Honors Program at the University of Cincinnati, Tim has also served as an adjunct professor and mentor to many college students and entrepreneurs. When he isn’t working or exploring with his wife, you’ll likely find him coaching or cheering on their four children at courts and fields around Cincinnati.

name: Tim Schigel
title: Managing Partner
bio:
Tim Schigel is an entrepreneur, investor, and connector who has spent his career helping founders turn bold ideas into high-growth companies. As the Founder and Managing Partner of Refinery Ventures, Tim focuses on helping entrepreneurs accelerate through the “early-scale” stage — the crucial phase between product-market fit and sustained hypergrowth.

Tim began his journey as a founder, creating ShareThis, one of the first social media platforms to reach over 500 million users worldwide. He later launched and led the Cintrifuse Syndicate Fund, a fund of funds backed by Cincinnati’s corporate community, where he built partnerships with leading venture firms and helped startups raise nearly $150 million.

Today, through Refinery Ventures and as a co-founder of the Great Lakes Venture Summit, Tim is dedicated to building stronger connections between the coasts and the Midwest. Drawing on his experience across Silicon Valley and the heartland, he shares actionable insights on leadership, scaling, and creating innovation ecosystems that last.

name: Tom Walker
title: Director of Industrial Design, VP, Partner
bio: Tom Walker is Vice President, Partner, and Director of Industrial Design at Mertz Design, where he leads the studio's industrial design practice in creating physical products that are as thoughtful in function as they are in form. Over 24 years in the field, he has developed products for brands including Crest, Oral-B, Zevo, and Rubbermaid. He helps businesses translate consumer insight into products, services, and strategies that solve real problems.

name: Torrey Babson
title: Senior Manager, Innovation Services
bio: Torrey Babson is the Senior Director of Innovation Services at BRITE Energy Innovators. Day-to-day, Torrey oversees BRITE's CXO Services, which provides fractional leadership solutions to pre-market energy technology startups.

name: Tracy Longley-Cook
title: Associate Professor of Art, School of Fine and Performing Arts

name: Trevor Paglen
title: Artist
bio:
Paglen has had solo exhibitions at the Smithsonian Museum of American Art, Washington D.C.; Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh, PA; Fondazione Prada, Milan, Italy; the Barbican Centre, London, UK; Vienna Secession, Austria; and Protocinema Istanbul, Turkey; and participated in group exhibitions at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, NY; the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, the Tate Modern, London, England; and numerous other venues.

Paglen has launched an artwork into distant orbit around Earth in collaboration with Creative Time and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), contributed research and cinematography to the Academy Award-winning film Citizenfour (2014), and created a radioactive public sculpture for the exclusion zone in Fukushima, Japan.

Paglen is the author of several books and many articles on subjects including experimental geography, artificial intelligence, state secrecy, military symbology, photography, and visuality. Paglen’s work has been profiled in the New York Times, The New Yorker,The Wall Street Journal, Wired, Financial Times, Artforum, and Aperture. In 2014, he received the Electronic Frontier Foundation’s Pioneer Award and, in 2016, he won the Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation Prize. Paglen was named a MacArthur Fellow in 2017.

In March 2026, Paglen was named the winner of the LG Guggenheim Award. Paglen’s sixth book, How to See Like a Machine: Images After AI, was released by Verso Books in the same year.

Paglen holds a B.A. from the University of California, Berkeley, an M.F.A. from the Art Institute of Chicago, and a Ph.D. in Geography from the University of California, Berkeley. (Photo Credit: Michael Avedon)
location: New York, NY and San Francisco, CA

name: Truly Design Crew
bio: Since getting up in train yards and abandoned factories, our production can now count anything from large scale murals to anamorphic artworks and painted basketball courts. The years spent in the fields of graffiti writing, street art and muralism shaped our attitude and allowed us to experiment new forms of visual language. We translate concepts and subjects through geometric abstraction. We have fun with different surfaces, deconstructing shapes and spaces and contaminating them with colors. Our artworks have inhabited walls in cities, museums, private homes and business headquarters in Italy and Europe, as well as in New York, Miami, Hong Kong and Macau.

name: Valerie Jacobs
title: Founder & CEO
bio:
Valerie Jacobs helps organizations see what's coming next, before everyone else does. As a trend forecaster and futurist, she has spent her career decoding shifts in culture, consumer behavior, and business, then turning that foresight into real growth. Over her career at LPK, she held several roles in the C-suite, using her forecasting instincts to help shape the direction of the company and its clients.

Today, through her own consultancy, Valerie Jacobs Futures, she works with organizations like The Coca-Cola Company, Nationwide, Fifth Third Bank, and The Milken Institute to help leaders build the kind of foresight that makes bold decisions feel a lot less risky. She holds a Master of Design from the University of Cincinnati, teaches trend forecasting there as an Adjunct Instructor, and serves as a Senior Fellow of the Design Futures Council. She has a long history with Cintrifuse, and her work has been featured in Forbes, Inc., and Vogue.

name: Vamos Animation
bio: VAMOS Animation is a German animation studio founded in 2016, organised as a collective of filmmakers, illustrators, artists, and animators with a strong track record at international film festivals and exhibitions. Bringing together diverse nationalities and cultural backgrounds, the collective approaches each project with a distinctly multicultural lens. The studio specialises in films and installations and, beyond classical animation, actively explores new formats and applications for animated sequences. In video mapping, the team has worked at events such as Berlin Festival of Lights (2023, 2024), the Video Mapping Festival in Amiens and Lille, and the mapping of the “Entrepôt des Sels” in Saint-Valery-sur-Somme (France), as well as projects in Cologne for theatre and other contexts. VAMOS stands out for integrating hand-drawn 2D animation with visual effects that serve the concept, prioritising narrative and social impact over mere spectacle.

name: VIGAS
bio: Vigas is a Brazilian multimedia artist known for his large-scale projections, light installations, 360 projections, and live performances. His practice explores the relationship between art, technology, and the environment, transforming public spaces into experiences that inspire new ways of perceiving both urban and natural landscapes.

name: Vince Fraser
bio: Vince Fraser is a pioneering British Afro-surrealist artist whose work sits at the intersection of digital art, visual storytelling, and cultural reclamation. With a career spanning over two decades, he has evolved from a successful commercial illustrator into a visionary digital artist known for immersive works that reimagine Black identity and heritage through an Afro-diasporic lens. Rooted in Afro-surrealism, his practice explores the spiritual, historical, and mythic dimensions of Black life in the present moment, blending photorealistic detail with African symbolism, surreal environments, and contemporary digital aesthetics.

name: Wayne Horse
bio: Willehad Eilers is a German artist also known under the pseudonym Wayne Horse, whose practice spans painting, drawing, video, and installation. Emerging from the German graffiti scene and later graduating from the Rijksakademie in Amsterdam, he continues to live and work in the Netherlands. His work is characterized by a raw, expressive visual language infused with humor and lyrical distortion, often exploring the bizarre, uncomfortable, and compelling aspects of contemporary human behavior. Through a practice that blends ethnographic observation with surreal reinterpretation, Eilers examines cultural and social norms, transforming everyday scenes into unsettling, poetic reflections on the modern condition.

name: William Butler-Croutwater
title: Managing Partner
bio: William Butler-Croutwater is a finance student at the University of Cincinnati and Managing Director of Bearcat Ventures. In his role, he works with students to develop their skills as early-stage investors while leading the organization’s approach to startup diligence and investing. His broader experience in venture capital has shaped an interest in how emerging technologies influence both company building and investment decisions. Outside of his work in venture, William serves in the Ohio Army National Guard.

name: William Thomas
title: Co-Founder & Partnerships Director (Cincinnati Art Week); Co-Founder & Principal, Cincy Nice
bio: Partnership builder and community strategist focused on bringing people and organizations together around ambitious ideas. William's experience spans fundraising, sponsorship development, operations, and relationship-building across cultural, civic, and neighborhood initiatives.
notes: CityBeat calls him "Billy" Thomas. Headshot = the shared co-founders photo in the "OUR TEAM" section of cincynice.com/about (two people, uncaptioned; see destinee-thomas). Also in the CAW team group photo: https://freight.cargo.site/t/original/i/T3056859355596179323774539701626/CINCYARTWEEK2067.png

name: Xavier University Art Department
bio: At Xavier University, the Art Department trains artists and thinkers who are grounded in integrity, intellectual curiosity, and a deep-seated sense of belonging. Innovation leads the curriculum. New materials, new contexts, and new audiences come together to push expectations; and Xavier Art students meet them. Between the traditional concentrations of fine Arts, the innovative Graphic Design Program, and the 3D Animation and Immersive Game Design Program, Xavier Art Students bring professional fluency, a portfolio of substance, and a habit of reflection that sustains careers in galleries, museums, design, education, and beyond.

name: Zac Strobl
title: Director
org: NKU Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship
bio: Zac Strobl is the Director of Northern Kentucky University’s Center for Innovation & Entrepreneurship and an entrepreneurship professor. He is a cofounder of The INKUBATOR, NKU’s award winning pre seed accelerator, and one of the founders of INVENT, a statewide startup internship program connecting students with emerging technology startups. His work focuses on developing entrepreneurial talent and strengthening connections between universities, startups, and the Greater Cincinnati tri-state region.

name: Zach Bahorik
title: Venture Partner
bio: https://fbtgibbons.com/people/zachary-d-bahorik/

name: Zachary Hensley
title: SVP, Product & Operations
bio: Zachary Hensley is SVP of Product & Operations at FRAYT, an early-stage tech startup building an on-demand logistics marketplace. He's spent 15+ years in tech and the last seven building venture-backed companies: COO and then President at Livegistics, and VP of Technology & Operations at Astronomer, where he was employee 19 and scaled the company through hypergrowth. Before startups, he was Head of Product at Kroger Digital and a Director at P&G, where he founded Alchemy, an internal startup. He's also an Expert in Residence at Cintrifuse Capital and an early member of X15 with Refinery Ventures.
